## 0. What this builds

### 0.1 One sentence
A new `bin/panel.mjs --fit` mode that (1) reconstructs each panel row's **app factor multipliers** for the fittable factor set — conforming to an explicit enumeration of each factor's **full input pipeline, walked to source data** (§3.0), not just its leaf transform — (2) fits per-position log-space **exponents** `wᵢ` over those multipliers with the hand-tuned stack (`wᵢ=1`) as a scale-corrected ridge prior, under the existing season-blocked forward-chaining CV, (3) compares the fitted-exponent pipeline against the hand-tuned (`wᵢ=1`) pipeline per position, and (4) writes a committed `grading/<date>-r3fit-verdict.md` with a per-position CLEARS / NO-GAIN / DEGRADES / UNSTABLE verdict and the fitted exponent vectors.

### 0.2 Fidelity is verified, not asserted (the governing premise)
The fit rests on **transportability**: exponents are fit on reconstructed multipliers, then shipped onto the *app's* multipliers, so a reconstruction must equal what the app computes for the same player-season or the fit tunes a model that is never served. Passes 1–3 found missed branches in the leaf transforms and in `seasonProjection.js`'s own routing; pass 4 re-scoped §3.0 to each factor's full input pipeline; pass 5 corrected the scoring-basis certification; pass 6 made the T-F10 gate hermetic.

**The reconstruction-fidelity enumeration is closed** (§3.0-C) and neither this pass nor any later one re-opens it. **The rule-0b strip is likewise closed** — global once-per-position selection, evaluated == shipped *support*. Pass 6 had made rule 0b train-fold-local out of an over-applied leakage instinct: `flatOneRate` is a **design-matrix-only** statistic — it never reads `outcomePPG` — so computing it over all rows is not outcome leakage and cannot inflate ΔMAE. Contrast the quantities that genuinely must stay train-only: `standardizeTrainApply`'s outcome mean and SD (`lib/panel.mjs:438-442`, consumed at `:447`) are functions of the target. The train-fold-local design bought nothing there and introduced a real defect: the evaluated parameterization could differ from the shipped one, so a CLEARS position could ship an exponent for a factor some fold held at 1.

**Fixing `F_p^fit` once per position buys `support`-identity, and that is the exact claim** (§0.3 Round 7 + item 50): the shipped refit and every scored fold draw from an **identical factor support** — same estimated set, same pinned set. It is **not** vector-identity: `wFinal` is an all-rows refit that no fold scored out of sample. State it at that strength everywhere it appears (§4, §8 item 1) — the activation unit cites §8 verbatim.

**Pass 9 (this revision) is a strictly-narrowing close-out.** It fixes **two verdict-validity holes** (the app's combined-factor clamp was absent from both arms; the log target had no positivity guard), **two one-line correctness gaps** (`teamRzShare`'s in-module 3dp rounding; the neutralization predicate's exact-zero trigger), and **removes six internal contradictions pass 8 introduced**. It **adds no new machinery** — no new factor sets, no new verdict channels, no new guards beyond tightening one existing predicate — and re-opens nothing settled.

39. **SUBSTANTIVE — rule 0b is ONE panel-level selection per position; the train-fold-local machinery is deleted (§4, §1, §3.2 step 6).**
    *Why the machinery was wrong, not just heavy:* `flatOneRate` is computed from the reconstructed factor columns alone and **never reads `outcomePPG`** — it is a property of the design matrix, so evaluating it over all panel rows leaks nothing about the target and cannot inflate ΔMAE. (The genuinely outcome-derived quantities — `standardizeTrainApply`'s `outcomeMean`/`outcomeSd`, `lib/panel.mjs:438-442` → `:447` — remain strictly train-only, untouched.) Meanwhile per-fold selection created a real defect: a factor pinned on every fold's train rows but estimated on the full panel would ship inside `wFinal` (§8 item 1) with ΔMAE evidence drawn from models that held it at 1.
    *The replacement:* `selectFitFactors(posRows, position)` runs **once per position** over that position's full fit-row set; the resulting `F_p^fit` is **fixed** and used **identically** by the shipped refit and by every CV fold and every α in the sweep. **Evaluated == shipped by construction.**
    *Deleted:* per-fold selection; `pinStability` (as gate or product); `flatOneRatesShipped` as a distinct returned value; the shipped-vs-fold pin distinction; and the T-F3/T-F4 assertions that existed only to police per-fold selection. *Kept:* the flat-1.0 definition (multiplier exactly 1.0 by any route), the pin-not-drop semantics (`wᵢ=1` in both arms), and sentinel/flat-1.0 counts as **reporting-only** diagnostics.

**Round 8 (this revision — the final substantive pass: one logic fix, one disposition fix, three claim folds, plus guard instrumentation):**
47. **SUBSTANTIVE — degenerate scale degrades gracefully per fold; it no longer aborts the run (§4; amends item 41; narrows item 34's collapse to the global scope where it holds).**
    *Why the abort was reachable, not belt-and-suspenders:* `selectFitFactors` runs **once globally** over `posRows`, but `s_i` is an **RMS scale computed per fold on that fold's train rows** (§1 step 2). A factor retained globally — flat-1.0 rate below 0.90 across the whole position — can be **100% flat on a single fold's train subset**, because a fold's train set is a proper subset of years. Then `s_i = 0` on that fold. Under the previous wording `fitExponents` threw, and one such fold **aborted the entire `--fit` run**. Item 34's redundancy argument (`s_i === 0 ⟺ flatOneRate === 1.0`, already pinned) is true **over the row set the selection saw** — it does not transfer to a fold's train subset, and that mismatch is exactly the reachable case. T-F3(d)'s old rationale ("unreachable for retained factors") was therefore **false**, and is corrected in §9.
    *The replacement:* the predicate stays **`Number.isFinite(s_i) && s_i > 0`**, but its failure branch **neutralizes that factor for that fold** — exponent fixed at 1, column excluded from that fold's design matrix — records it in the fold diagnostics, and **the run proceeds**. Two distinct recorded reasons, because they mean different things: a degenerate-scale reason (an expected, benign thin-fold event) and `nonFiniteScale` (`s_i` non-finite; only reachable via a reconstructed multiplier of exactly 0 or ∞, which all seven app clamps forbid — a **fidelity failure**, folded into §7's expect-0 assertion set beside `zeroGpWithStats` and `nonFiniteFantasyPoints`, not laundered into a benign counter). ***Amended by item 57:*** the degenerate-scale **trigger** is no longer the exact-zero test `s_i === 0` and its reason is no longer named `degenerateScale` — it is a **rate test** on the fold's train rows reusing `FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE`, recorded as **`flatOnTrain`**, because exact-zero missed the near-degenerate fold. `Number.isFinite(s_i) && s_i > 0` survives as an assertion behind it. §4 is authoritative.
    *Where it cannot fire:* the shipped all-rows refit (§4 step 5). There `s_i === 0` **does** imply `flatOneRate === 1.0 ≥ 0.90`, so the factor was already pinned — item 34's collapse holds at that scope. A neutralization on the shipped refit is therefore a hard **stop-and-investigate**, not a degradation.
48. **FIDELITY/DISPOSITION — QB `rzUsageFactor` is HELD-IN-ARM, not absent (§2, §3.0-B6, §3.2, §5, §9, §11).** `RZ_CONFIG.QB` exists (`usageMetrics.js:59` — `pass_rz_att`/`pass_att`, `minOpp 50`, `shrinkK 80`), QB has a real `rz` cohort pool (`:75`, gated `:96`), and `computeUsageFactors` is called **unposition-gated** on the veteran path (`seasonProjection.js:476-479`) with `rzUsageFactor` entering `combinedNewFactorRaw` for **every** position (`:594-597`). So `rzUsageFactor` is a genuine non-neutral multiplier on the QB veteran path. §2 dispositioned it "FIT (RB/WR/TE)" with **no QB row**, which would have left it out of `F_QB^full` — i.e. out of `predHand` — making the QB verdict apples-to-oranges against an app arm that applies it. **Disposition: HELD-IN-ARM** — reconstructed, carried in **both** QB arms at `wᵢ = 1`, never a fit candidate. Not fitted because QB is underpowered (§5) and holding keeps the comparison honest without spending a parameter. *Coverage is real, not marginal:* `pass_att ≥ 50` clears for ~81–85 QBs/season (2018/2021/2024) and `pass_rz_att` is present for ~94–109. **§2 gains the HELD row and a disposition legend; §5 gains the QB held-in-arm line.**

## 1. The model form + the fit (settled — assessment §B.1(2); scale-corrected)

Per position `p`, over the **product set** `F_p^full` (§2):

```
projectedPPG = basePPG × Π_{i∈F_p^full} fᵢ^{wᵢ}        (held/omitted factors: implicitly wᵢ = 1 / absent)
```

**Three nested sets — product, candidates, estimated (rule 0b, §0.3 items 23/39/48).**
```
F_p^full        ⊇  FIT_CANDIDATES[p]      ⊇  F_p^fit
(both arms)        (eligible to be fit)      (exponents actually estimated)
```
- **`F_p^full`** — the product set (§2). Every member contributes to **both** `predHand` and `predFitted`.
- **`FIT_CANDIDATES[p]`** — the members eligible for estimation. `F_p^full \ FIT_CANDIDATES[p]` are **HELD-IN-ARM by disposition** (config, decided here): in both arms at `wᵢ = 1`, never estimated. In v1 this is exactly `{QB: rzUsage}` (§2, §0.3 item 48).
- **`F_p^fit`** — chosen **once per position** by `selectFitFactors` over `FIT_CANDIDATES[p]` on that position's full fit-row set (§4), then **fixed**. `FIT_CANDIDATES[p] \ F_p^fit` are **pinned by rule 0b** (data, decided at run time): also `wᵢ = 1`, also in both arms.

Held-in-arm and pinned are arithmetically identical (`wᵢ = 1`, both arms) and differ only in provenance — config vs data. The verdict reports them separately so a reader can tell which is which.

The fixed `F_p^fit` is used by every CV fold, every α in the sweep, and the shipped refit, so **the shipped refit and every scored fold draw from an identical factor support** — support-identity, not vector-identity (§0.2, §8 item 1). One bounded per-fold exception is reported, never silent: §4's graceful degenerate-scale neutralization.

**Never drop a pinned or held-in-arm factor from `predHand`:** the hand arm must stay the app's true hand-tuned prediction, including on the rows where that factor is not 1.0.

**Positivity precondition — drop before taking a log (§0.3 item 55).** Both logs below are undefined at 0. A `0`-point row **reaches this formula**: `buildHalfPprOutcomes` coerces `rec.fantasyPoints ?? 0` (`scripts/grade-snapshot.mjs:74`) and `buildPanelRow` tests only `ppg == null` / `gamesPlayed < minOutcomeGames` / `!Number.isFinite(ppg)` (`lib/panel.mjs:246-250`) — **never positivity**. So, before forming `y`, **drop any row with `outcomePPG ≤ 0` or `anchorBasePPG ≤ 0`**, under the counted reasons `nonPositiveOutcome` / `nonPositiveAnchor` (§3.2 step 4a, reported in `fitCoverage`).

*Why a drop and not a clamp or an epsilon:* a 0-ppg outcome carries no ratio information — `log(actual/predHand)` is `−∞` however it is floored — and flooring it would inject a large fabricated negative residual that a no-intercept fit would absorb into the `δ`s. Drop, count, report.

*Why it must be an explicit guard rather than a trusted invariant:* the failure is **silent**. A `NaN` target yields `NaN` betas, and `solveOLS`' singularity test is `if (maxVal < 1e-10)` (`lib/backtest.mjs:63`) — `Math.abs(NaN)` is `NaN` and **`NaN < 1e-10` is `false`**, so the pivot check passes and the solve returns `singular: false` with an all-`NaN` `beta`. Every downstream MAE, ΔMAE and Spearman becomes `NaN` with no error raised and no flag set. Expected incidence at the gp≥6 gates is 0 or near-0, which is why T-F19 asserts it certified-inert-style rather than the hot path defending against it (§3.0 stop rule does **not** fire on this — it is enumerated).

**Target (per position, per CV fold) — the hand-stack log-residual, no intercept, no basePPG exponent:**
```
y(r) = log(outcomePPG(r)) − log(anchorBasePPG(r)) − Σ_{i∈F_p^full} log fᵢ(r)     // = log( actual / predHand_unclamped )
```
`predHand_unclamped = anchorBasePPG × Π_{i∈F_p^full} fᵢ` (all `wᵢ=1`; pinned and held-in-arm factors included). `basePPG` is the fixed anchor. Both `outcomePPG` and `anchorBasePPG` come from the **same half-PPR outcome maps** (§3.0-C3) — the app's own basis — so `y` carries no scale offset between arms.

**The target is deliberately the UNCLAMPED residual (§0.3 item 54).** The app's combined-factor envelope (below) is a **non-linear post-transform**; folding it into `y` would destroy the log-linear form the OLS rests on. The fit is therefore **unconstrained in log space and constrained at scoring** — the standard decomposition, and the one that makes ΔMAE measure the app's real objective. The envelope is measured inert in the hand arm (0/1,504, `seasonProjection.js:584`), so this costs essentially nothing on the hand side; §7 reports realized clamp-hit rates per arm rather than assuming it. **No centering / no intercept:** the multiplicative model has no additive term, and `y` is ~zero-mean because the hand stack is roughly log-unbiased. **Monitor:** report `mean_r(y)` per position; if `|mean(y)| > 0.03` flag it — a no-intercept fit would otherwise absorb a basePPG miscalibration into the `δ`s, which is a separate question, not something the exponent fit should launder.

**Regressors + scale-corrected ridge:**
1. Raw regressors `x_i(r) = log fᵢ(r)` **for `i ∈ F_p^fit` only** — tiny and unequal-variance (factors sit near 1; `shareTrend` varies far more than `teamRzShare`). A constant ridge on raw columns shrinks by wildly different *fractions* per factor and crushes the low-variance, best-grounded ones — so **scale first**.
2. **Per fold, train rows only:** uncentered RMS scale `s_i = sqrt( (1/nTrain) Σ_{r∈train} x_i(r)² )`, `x'_i = x_i / s_i`. Uncentered preserves the no-intercept semantics (origin stays at `log f = 0 ⟺ w = 1`). Each scaled train column then has Gram diagonal exactly `nTrain` (`solveOLS` builds `XᵀX`, `lib/backtest.mjs:32-47`). *(The scales are train-local because they are fitted nuisance parameters; the factor **set** is fixed globally because it is a design-matrix property — §0.3 item 39.)*
3. Fit `y ≈ Σ_i β_i x'_i` via **`solveOLS(X', y, { ridgeLambda: α · nTrain })`** — ridge adds `ridgeLambda` to each Gram diagonal (`lib/backtest.mjs:47`), so each regularized diagonal is `nTrain(1+α)`. **Claim scope:** RMS scaling **equalizes each factor's scale**, making `α` dimensionless and `n`-independent; the shrinkage is exactly the uniform fraction `1/(1+α)` **only under column orthogonality**. The fitted factors are correlated (the usage trio; momentum/trajectory), so off-diagonal Gram terms leave per-coefficient shrinkage slightly non-uniform — second-order and unavoidable. The defect this fixes is the **scale** non-uniformity.
4. Map back: `δ_i = β_i / s_i` (train `s_i`); **`w_i = 1 + δ_i`** for `i ∈ F_p^fit`, **`w_i = 1`** for pinned factors. Ridge toward `β=0` ⟺ `δ=0` ⟺ **`w=1`**. `w_i≈0` = "empirically dead"; `w_i≈1` = "hand-tuned was right". Low-variance factors are amplified in raw `δ` but their prediction effect stays bounded (`δ·log f` with tiny `log f`), and the app's `combinedNewFactor` clamp `[0.67,1.50]` still guards the product.

**Prediction on an eval fold — TWO clamps, both arms, identical rows/folds/product set (§0.3 item 54).**

The app does not multiply a flat product into `rawPPG`. It splits the stack: ten factors go into `combinedNewFactorRaw`, that product is **clamped to `[0.67, 1.50]`**, and only then does it join the un-enveloped terms:
```
// app, seasonProjection.js:594-601
combinedNewFactorRaw = qbQuality · momentum · breakout · bounceBack · tdReliance
                     · trajectory · efficiency · snapShare · rzUsage · teamRzShare   // :594-597
combinedNewFactor    = clamp(combinedNewFactorRaw, 0.67, 1.50)                       // :598  ← INNER
rawPPG               = basePPG · ageDelta · shareTrend · regression
                     · teamFactor · depthFactor · combinedNewFactor                  // :599-600
pipelinePPG          = clamp(rawPPG, 0, 40)                                          // :601  ← OUTER
```
**Partition `F_p^full` accordingly** — `ENVELOPE_FACTORS = {momentum, trajectory, snapShare, rzUsage, teamRzShare}` (5 of the 7 fitted; the envelope's other five members are all HELD-OMITTED, hence 1.0 in the reduced pipeline), and the remainder `{shareTrend, regression}` multiplies in directly:
```
inner(r, w) = clamp( exp( Σ_{i ∈ F_p^full ∩ ENVELOPE_FACTORS} w_i · log fᵢ(r) ), 0.67, 1.50 )
outer(r, w) =        exp( Σ_{i ∈ F_p^full \ ENVELOPE_FACTORS} w_i · log fᵢ(r) )

predFitted(r) = clamp( anchorBasePPG(r) · outer(r, w) · inner(r, w), 0, 40 )   // w_i = 1 for pinned / held-in-arm i
predHand(r)   = clamp( anchorBasePPG(r) · outer(r, 1) · inner(r, 1), 0, 40 )
```
For QB this is `inner` over `{momentum, trajectory, rzUsage}` and `outer` over `{regression}` — `shareTrend` is not in `F_QB^full` at all (§5, §0.3 item 62).

**Why the inner clamp is load-bearing even though it is inert in the hand arm.** Measured at `[0.67,1.50]` it fires **0 times in 1,504** qualifying vet projections (`:584`), so `predHand` is unaffected. But `wᵢ > 1` amplifies each `log fᵢ`, so the **fitted** arm can leave an envelope the hand arm never approaches. Omitting it would let the fitted arm bank lift **the app truncates in production** — ΔMAE biased toward the fitted arm, invisibly, in a way no gate rule catches. The app itself flags the headroom as thin at ten factors (`:587-589`). Applying it in **both** arms is what makes ΔMAE measure the app's real objective.

**Named limitation, reported not assumed.** The reduced pipeline reconstructs 5 of the envelope's 10 members, so the reconstructed `inner` is a **narrower** product than production's and fires **less often** than the app's would. It catches the fitted arm's own inflation — the risk above — but not full production clamp incidence. §7 prints **clamp-hit counts per arm per position** so a CLEARS driven by heavy fitted-arm clamping is visible rather than inferred.

Comp blend (Step 9) is out of both arms (§5). `w_i` are raw-space exponents recovered on train `s_i`, applied to raw eval `log fᵢ` — leakage-safe. A pinned or held-in-arm factor contributes the identical term to both arms, so it cancels in `ΔMAE` while keeping the hand baseline true. **Both clamps are order-sensitive: apply `inner` before multiplying, never fold the two into one range.**

## 2. The fittable factor set (per position) + what is held

| Factor (app) | app source | v1 disposition | why |

| comp blend (Step 9) | — | **out (both arms)** | kNN port out of scope |

**Disposition legend — four dispositions, two of which are arithmetically identical (§1, §0.3 item 48):**

| Disposition | In `F_p^full`? | In both arms? | Estimable? | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FIT** | yes | yes | yes — a `FIT_CANDIDATES` member | config (§2) |
| **HELD-IN-ARM** | yes | yes, at `wᵢ = 1` | **no** | config (§2) — v1: QB `rzUsage` only |
| **pinned** (rule 0b) | yes | yes, at `wᵢ = 1` | was a candidate; removed | **data**, at run time (§4) |
| **HELD-OMITTED / HELD (hard block) / HELD v1** | **no** | **no — out of both arms** | no | config (§2); this is the reduced-pipeline limitation (§5) |

Do not collapse HELD-IN-ARM into HELD-OMITTED: the first keeps the app's multiplier in the hand baseline, the second removes it from both arms. QB `rzUsage` is the former precisely because the app applies it.

**v1 `F_p^full` (the product set — both arms):** RB/WR/TE = `{shareTrend, regression, momentum, trajectory, snapShare, rzUsage, teamRzShare}` (**7**). QB = `{momentum, regression, trajectory, rzUsage}` (**4**).

**v1 `FIT_CANDIDATES` (eligible for estimation):** RB/WR/TE = the same **7**. QB = `{momentum, regression, trajectory}` (**3**) — `rzUsage` is HELD-IN-ARM.

`F_p^fit` is `FIT_CANDIDATES[p]` minus whatever `selectFitFactors` pins for that position (§4) — decided once, then fixed. **QB is the only position where `F_p^full` and `FIT_CANDIDATES` differ in v1**; keep the two constants distinct anyway, so the next held-in-arm factor is a data edit rather than a refactor.

**Not in the set:** `shareLevel` is an **E-0a candidate feature**, not an app factor — it has no multiplier in `computeNextSeasonProjection` and cannot receive an exponent. Its 2026-08-08 CLEARS on WR/RB is a separate finding (header scope note); this unit neither reads nor activates it.

**Omitted-variable caveat (state in the verdict):** omitting `efficiencyFactor` risks the usage exponents partially proxying for per-opportunity efficiency. The app treats usage and efficiency as orthogonal multipliers and validated `teamRzShare`'s partial-β after controlling for usage (not efficiency), so the OVB is expected modest; the ridge-toward-1 prior caps drift. **Efficiency is the named stage-2 priority** — the §3 registry admits it as one function + one entry.

**Design the sets as data**, in `lib/panel.mjs` — **`FULL_FACTORS` + `FIT_CANDIDATES` + `ENVELOPE_FACTORS`, per §6.2, which is the single authority for their names and shapes.** *(The earlier single-`FIT_FACTORS` instruction that stood here is deleted — it contradicted §6.2 and would have collapsed the product set into the candidate set, which is the defect §0.3 item 48 fixed. §0.3 item 58.)*

## 3. Factor-multiplier reconstruction — `lib/projectionFactors.mjs` (NEW, pure)

Cross-repo **mirror contract** (like `lib/fantasyPoints.mjs` mirrors `src/utils/fantasyPoints.js`) — §11.

### 3.0 Input-pipeline parity — enumerate the app's full chains FIRST (the method)

Every reconstruction below conforms to this enumeration. Read the app source read-only at the cited anchors; do not edit it. The unit of enumeration is **the factor's entire input pipeline**, not its leaf transform: transform → series/cohort construction → upstream aggregation → terminal source file.

#### A. Path routing — which players get the fitted factors at all

```
computeNextSeasonProjection (seasonProjection.js:245)
├─ :265-266  guard      !player || !SKILL.has(position) → return null       [panel: PANEL_POSITIONS already restricts]
├─ :283-303  qualifying = seasons with finite gamesPlayed ≥ 8 AND finite fantasyPoints,
│                          ascending, ppg = fantasyPoints / gamesPlayed
├─ :310      ROUTING    qualifying.length === 0 || (yearsExp != null && yearsExp <= 1) → rookieProjection
└─ else      VETERAN path :315-737 (the only path that computes the fitted factors)
```

Rookie factors object (`:198-237`) versus the seven fitted factors:

| Fitted factor | Rookie path | Veteran path |
|---|---|---|
| `shareTrend` | **hardcoded 1.0** (`:201`) | computed `:340-361` |
| `regressionFactor` | **hardcoded 1.0** (`:202`) | computed `:363-384` |
| `teamRzShareFactor` | **hardcoded 1.0** (`:235`) | computed `:481-497` |
| `momentumFactor` | **absent (key not present)** | `:386-394` |
| `trajectoryFactor` | **absent** | `:461-465` |
| `snapShareFactor` | **absent** | `:471-479` |
| `rzUsageFactor` | **absent** | `:471-479` |

⇒ **No fitted exponent is ever applied on the rookie path.** Fitting on rookie-path rows trains weights against a cohort the app never applies them to.

**Exclusion rule R1 (both disjuncts).** Drop a row from the fit when either holds; count each separately:
- `qualifyingSeasons.length === 0` → reason `rookiePathNoQualifying` (disjunct 1, exact).
- The player has **no season-totals appearance in any season < Y** → reason `rookiePathYearsExpProxy` (disjunct 2, proxy).

*Why a proxy:* `years_exp` is in no served file — roster carries `{team, position, status, fullName}`, and `draft_picks` has no server-side `sleeper_id` join (the same gap that makes the baseline age-blind, roadmap R1-AGE). A player debuting in season Y has completed one season at the Y→Y+1 offseason when the app projects, i.e. `years_exp = 1` → rookie path.

*Error direction (state honestly):* the proxy is **conservative** — it also excludes a player rostered-but-statless before Y (true `years_exp ≥ 2`; the app would use the veteran path). Those rows are **lost, not corrupted**. Count them where distinguishable and report.

*Boundary ambiguity + its escalation:* whether Sleeper flips `years_exp` at the season rollover decides whether a player who debuted in **Y−1** reads `1` (rookie path) or `2` (veteran path) at projection time. Report the count of debut-in-`Y−1` rows as a **sensitivity cohort**, and run the fit twice — including and excluding them. If any position's verdict label differs between the two runs, report that position **UNSTABLE**; never pick the favourable run. **The override lives in `runFit` (§6.3), not in `decideFitVerdict` (§4)** — the sensitivity label is the output of a second full grading pass, so it cannot be an input to the function that pass itself calls (§0.3 item 49).

#### B. Per-factor branch table — every flat-1.0 the app can return, plus input construction

A **sentinel** is a value the app *computes as 1.0*; it is **not** a row drop. Reproducing a sentinel as a drop silently changes the fit population; reproducing a drop as a 1.0 injects fake neutrals. Both are wrong; the table below is the authority. Rows numbered `N-S` enumerate the **construction of a factor's input series**, whose per-entry drops are *series* drops, never row drops. *(A sentinel is one way a multiplier lands on exactly 1.0; it is not the only way — see rule 0b's `flatOneRate`, §4.)*

#### C. Closure statement — per-factor input-chain certification

**Certification standard.** A factor's chain is *certified* when every node from its transform down to the terminal source file is either **(i) reproduced**, **(ii) certified inert** with a stated mechanism plus a cheap assertion, or **(iii) named below** as a residual or a measured divergence. A chain that terminates at a function nobody walked is **not** certified — see the stop rule.

| Factor | Transform (walked) | Upstream producers walked | Terminal source | Chain status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `momentum` | `momentum.js:18-35` ← `seasonProjection.js:364-365, 386-394` | `qualifying` builder `:283-303` (gp≥8 + finite `fantasyPoints`) → `careerStats` ← `loadCareerHistory` `sleeperStats.js:237-267` (2012 floor `:240`) ← store read `:145-159` **verbatim** / live-API aggregation `:184-228` | `nfl/season-totals/<year>.json` v3 (`fantasyPoints` = half-PPR, `gamesPlayed`) | reproduced; basis matched by construction → **C3**; finite-`fantasyPoints` skip → **C6** |
| `regression` | `regressionSignals.js:72-78` + `seasonProjection.js:363-384` | same `qualifying` chain (`careerAvg` `:364`, `lastPPG` `:366`) | same | reproduced; **C3**, **C6** |
| `trajectory` | `regressionSignals.js:48-60` ← `:461-465` | same `qualifying` chain (`ppgs` `:365`) | same | reproduced; **C3**, **C6** |
| `shareTrend` | `computeShareTrend` `teamContext.js:314-348` + `seasonProjection.js:340-361` | **series** `computeHistoricalShares` `:269-308` (`App.jsx:210-213`) → **denominators** `computeHistoricalTeamTotals` `:240-260` (`App.jsx:205-207`) → `careerStats` (as above) + `playersMap` | season-totals v3 + Sleeper players directory | series reproduced (§3.4, row 4-S); denominator gp≥1 gate → **C4**; `rec` accumulator → **C5**; playersMap position → **C2**; per-season team fallback → **C1**; membership gate certified inert (below) |
| `snapShare` | `usageMetrics.js:137-155` ← `:471-479` | own counts `careerStats[lastQ.season][pid].stats` (`:407-408`, `:479`); **pool** `buildUsageCohortTable:71-104` (refSeason `:72`, position `playersMap[pid].position` `:81`, gate `:89`) + cache `:106-112` | season-totals v3 + directory | reproduced; pool position source → **C2** |
| `rzUsage` | `usageMetrics.js:157-176` | same own-count chain; **pool** `:93-97` (gate `opp ≥ minOpp` `:96`) | same | reproduced; **C2** |
| `teamRzShare` | `teamRzShare.js:127-169` ← `:481-497` | own counts (`:408`, `:490`); **team resolution at the call site** `resolveAttributedTeam(lastSeasonRaw, player, attribution)` `seasonProjection.js:488` → `teamContext.js:18-21`; **cohort** `buildCohortTable:68-99` + cache `:101-108`; **denominators** `computeHistoricalTeamTotals:240-260` | season-totals v3 + directory | reproduced; **C1**, **C2**, **C4**, **C5** (inert for this factor — it reads `rushRz`/`recRz`) |

**Certified inert (no code, mechanism stated).** `computeHistoricalShares`' playersMap-membership gate (`teamContext.js:278`) cannot exclude a row's own share series: the app can only project a player it found in `playersMap` (`:265-266`), so `playersMap[playerId]` is non-null for every player whose series Step 3 reads. It gates only *other* players' series, which the projection never consumes.

**No fitted factor's chain terminates at an un-walked function.** Every node above resolves to reproduced code, a C1–C7 entry, or the certified-inert item. *(The table enumerates each factor's **input** chain; C7 covers the **downstream** combination step the app applies to five of the seven outputs — §0.3 item 54.)*

Named residuals, measured divergences, and certified-inert differences:

1. **RESIDUAL — `resolveAttributedTeam` current-team fallback (not reproducible).** In `per-season-team` mode the app resolves `seasonEntry?.team ?? player?.team ?? null` (`teamContext.js:19`) — it **falls back to the current team** when a season record carries no `team`. The panel's `teamKeyResolver` per-season-team branch is `totalsByYear[season]?.[pid]?.team ?? null` (`lib/panel.mjs:57-59`) — **no fallback**, by design (the R2 flip gate's semantics). Consequence: for a season record with `team == null`, the app may compute a real `teamRzShare` (and include the player in the cohort pool, and keep that season in the share series) where the reconstruction ships the `!playerTeam` sentinel (1.0), drops them from the pool (`teamRzShare.js:86`), and drops the season from the series (`teamContext.js:282`).
   - *Expected materiality:* the fallback exists for live-API-aggregated seasons and v1/v2 cache entries (app comment `teamContext.js:3-8`); the panel reads **store-served v3 files**, which carry per-season `team`. So it should be near-inert — **but measure, don't assume**: count fit rows and cohort-pool members whose `lastQSeason` record has `team == null`, plus share-series seasons dropped for the same reason, per position, and report in the verdict.
   - *Escalation:* if that count exceeds **1% of a position's fit rows**, listwise-drop those rows (reason `nullSeasonTeam`) rather than let a sentinel-vs-computed divergence sit silently in the fit, and say so in the verdict.
2. **MEASURED — position source (two consumption points).** The app takes position from `playersMap[pid].position` — for cohort pools (`usageMetrics.js:81`, `teamRzShare.js:76`) **and** for the share series' RB-vs-WR/TE branch (`teamContext.js:279-280`). The panel uses `resolvePosition(pid, advstatsY, rosterY)` (`lib/panel.mjs:98-106`), resolved at Y and (per §3.4) applied to every season of the series, mirroring the app's single-position-for-all-seasons behaviour. Pool composition can differ slightly → a one-point `percentileRank` shift. Not reproducible (no playersMap server-side). Report per position-year pool sizes; budget it in T-F10's tolerance (§9) — **no new tolerance for the second consumption point**; it is the same divergence, reported once. *(Both exclude `TEAM_*` from pools — the app because `playersMap['TEAM_KC']` is undefined, the panel because advstats/roster carry no such id.)*
3. **CORRECTED, then ELIMINATED BY CONSTRUCTION — scoring basis (§0.3 item 26).** `getSeasonTotals` returns the data-store file **verbatim** (`src/api/sleeperStats.js:145-159`) — no re-scoring — and the data repo writes `weeklyPoints[week] = stats.pts_half_ppr ?? 0` (`lib/sleeper.mjs:212`), `fantasyPoints` = their rounded sum, `scoringBasis = 'half_ppr'` (`:240-243`). The app reads `d.fantasyPoints` directly (`seasonProjection.js:290, 298`). League scoring enters `careerStats` **only** on the live-API fallback (`sleeperStats.js:199`; the `App.jsx:788-795` call sites are current-week/display, never careerStats). ⇒ **the app's projection ppg series is half-PPR regardless of the league's custom scoring.**
   - *Consequence — the fit runs `--basis half_ppr` (§6.3).* `buildHalfPprOutcomes` reads `rec.fantasyPoints` verbatim and returns `fp / gp` (`scripts/grade-snapshot.mjs:70-81`) — the identical fields and arithmetic the app uses ⇒ **exact parity by construction**. Under `--basis in-basis` the panel recomputes points from `stats` under the snapshot's custom scoring (`:87-115`), producing a series the app never used, **and** a systematic scale offset between an in-basis outcome and a half-PPR-denominated hand prediction, which a no-intercept fit absorbs into the `δ`s.
   - *Bonus:* `--basis half_ppr` needs no snapshot (`resolveScoring:58-59`), dropping the pinned-`2026-07-05` scoring dependency.
   - *Cost, stated honestly in the verdict:* the fit optimizes half-PPR accuracy, which is the **self-consistent** choice — the app's own `projectedPPG` is half-PPR-denominated on store-served data, so exponents are fit in the units they are applied in. *(Note the 2026-08-08 E-0a baseline runs `basis=custom`, `attribution=current-team`; the fit deliberately differs on both, so §5's counts are indicative of panel scale, not of the fit's exact row set.)*
   - *Named residual (not measurable server-side):* a season a client served from its **live-API fallback** carries league scoring in that client's cache. The fallback fires only when the store has no usable manifest entry or the fetch fails — a transient-failure state, invisible to the harness. Named, not measured.
   - *Unchanged elsewhere:* E-0a and the flip gate keep their in-basis convention; **only `--fit` defaults differently**.
4. **CERTIFIED INERT (with assertion) — the denominator `gamesPlayed ≥ 1` gate.** `computeHistoricalTeamTotals` skips contributors with `gamesPlayed < 1` (`teamContext.js:245`); `buildTeamTotalsForSeason` has no such gate. *Mechanism:* both aggregators accumulate stat keys **only inside the played-week branch** (data `lib/sleeper.mjs:208-217`; app `src/api/sleeperStats.js:195-203`), so a `gamesPlayed === 0` record carries no positive stat keys and adds 0 to every denominator. *Assertion (T-F18b):* over the loaded years, count records with `gamesPlayed === 0` **and** any of `rush_att`/`rec_tgt`/`rec`/`rush_rz_att`/`rec_rz_tgt` > 0; expect **0** and report. If ever non-zero, add the gate and re-run — do not absorb it.
5. **CLOSED BY AN ADDITIVE LINE — the `rec` denominator.** The app's WR/TE fallback divides by `teamTotals.rec` (`teamContext.js:297`, accumulated `:252`); the panel builder tracks no `rec` (`lib/panel.mjs:77-82`). Closed in §6.2 by one additive accumulator — not a residual.
6. **CERTIFIED INERT (narrow guarantee + assertion) — the non-finite/absent `fantasyPoints` skip (§0.3 items 37, 44).** The app drops a season from `qualifying` when `!Number.isFinite(d.fantasyPoints)` (`seasonProjection.js:290-295`), even at `gamesPlayed ≥ 8`. The panel's step-1 test is "finite `ppg` and `gp ≥ 8`" (§3.2), and `buildHalfPprOutcomes` coerces a missing value — `const fp = rec.fantasyPoints ?? 0` (`scripts/grade-snapshot.mjs:74`) — so such a record would yield a **finite ppg of 0** and be *kept* where the app drops it.
   *Mechanism, stated at its true strength:* two independent guarantees, covering different failure modes. (a) **Non-finite** values cannot reach a published file: `validateNflSeason` (`lib/validate.mjs:100`) runs `findNonFinite` per player and **throws rather than publish** (`:120-128`; helper `:69-88`). (b) **Absent** values are *not* covered by that validator — `findNonFinite` inspects only `typeof value === 'number'` (`:70-71`), so a missing key passes it silently; that half rests solely on `lib/sleeper.mjs:240-242`, which assigns `fantasyPoints` a rounded number for **every** player in `totals`. Because (b) is a single-point guarantee, the counter below is what makes it safe rather than assumed.
   *Assertion (T-F18c):* while building `qualifyingSeasons`, count records with `gamesPlayed ≥ 8` whose raw `fantasyPoints` is **absent or non-finite**; expect **0**, report the count, and if ever non-zero add the explicit finite-`fantasyPoints` test to step 1 and re-run. Enumerated so §3.0's stop rule does not halt the implementer on a known-inert difference.

7. **REPRODUCED (not a residual, not inert) — the combined-factor envelope (§0.3 item 54).** The veteran path does **not** multiply the fitted factors into `rawPPG` as one flat product. Five of the seven — `momentum`, `trajectory`, `snapShare`, `rzUsage`, `teamRzShare` — enter `combinedNewFactorRaw` (`seasonProjection.js:594-597`), which is **clamped to `[0.67, 1.50]`** (`:598`) before joining `basePPG · ageDelta · shareTrend · regression · teamFactor · depthFactor` in `rawPPG` (`:599-600`); `clamp(rawPPG, 0, 40)` (`:601`) is a **second, outer** clamp. The remaining two fitted factors (`shareTrend`, `regression`) sit outside the envelope.
   *Status:* **reproduced in both arms** — §1's `inner`/`outer` partition. It is *not* certified inert: it is measured inert in the **hand** arm (0/1,504 at this range, `:584`) and is precisely where the **fitted** arm can bind, since `wᵢ > 1` amplifies `log fᵢ`.
   *Residual within the reproduction, named:* the envelope's other five members (`qbQuality`, `breakout`, `bounceBack`, `tdReliance`, `efficiency`) are HELD-OMITTED (§2), so the reconstructed envelope wraps five factors where production wraps ten and therefore **fires less often**. Measured, not assumed — §7 reports clamp-hit rates per arm per position.

**Closure sentence (corrected — §0.3 item 54).** Nothing else in the veteran path, or in any of the seven input chains, branches on anything the fitted factors **consume**. What the prior wording missed is that the veteran path does something to what the fitted factors **produce**: the `[0.67, 1.50]` envelope at `seasonProjection.js:598` is a transform *downstream* of five of the seven multipliers, so a chain-input enumeration could not surface it. It is now enumerated as **C7** and reproduced. **Stop rule:** if the implementer finds a further branch — in a transform, a series/cohort builder, an upstream aggregation, **or a downstream combination step between a factor and `pipelinePPG`** — **stop and report**; do not paper it with an imputed neutral. (C1–C7 are already enumerated; a difference matching one of those is not a stop, and neither is the non-positive-ppg drop of §0.3 item 55, which T-F19 asserts.)

### 3.1 Exports (signatures)
```js
// Bucket factors — deterministic from the player's full qualifying history (no cohort).
export function reconstructMomentumFactor(ppgs, meanPPG) → number            // <4 qualifying → 1.0 (§3.0-B1)
export function reconstructRegressionFactor(ppgs, meanPPG, lastPPG) → number // no sentinel; <3 → undampened (§3.0-B2)
export function reconstructTrajectoryFactor(ppgs) → number                   // <2 or non-finite → 1.0 (§3.0-B3)
export function reconstructShareTrendMultiplier(shareSeries) → number         // <2 seasons → 1.0 (§3.0-B4)

// shareTrend's INPUT SERIES — mirrors computeHistoricalShares (teamContext.js:269-308), NOT
// the panel's computeShare. Returns [{ season, share (3dp), gamesPlayed }] oldest→newest;
// a season that fails any per-season condition is ABSENT, never a 0 (§3.0-B4-S, §3.4).
export function reconstructShareSeries({ pid, position, seasons, totalsByYear, teamTotalsByYear })
  → { series: Array<{season, share, gamesPlayed}>, dropped: { belowGp8, nullTeam, noTeamEntry, zeroOwnVolume, nonFinite } }

// Cohort-percentile factors — player counts from lastQ.season, pool from season Y (§3.2).
// Raw COUNTS required (the app shrinks the percentile by sample size). Each returns the app's
// computed 1.0 on its sentinel conditions (§3.0-B5/6/7) — never signals a drop.
export function reconstructSnapShareFactor({ offSnp, tmOffSnp }, cohortSnapShares) → number
// position selects RZ_CONFIG — ALL FOUR positions, QB included (usageMetrics.js:58-64).
// `rzOwn` is the ?? 0 coalescence, not a drop: absent RZ key + positive opp = a real rate of 0.
export function reconstructRzUsageFactor({ rzOwn, opp }, cohortRates, position) → number
// Returns the factor ROUNDED TO 3dp — teamRzShare.js:166 rounds in-module, before the
// factor enters the product. Do NOT stop at the clamp: unlike snapShare/rzUsage (whose
// factors enter unrounded), skipping this shifts every teamRzShare multiplier AND drops a
// flat-1.0 route ([0.9995,1.0005) → 1.000) that rule 0b's pin decision reads (§0.3 item 56).
export function reconstructTeamRzShareFactor({ rzOwn, opp, teamDenom }, cohortShares, position) → number

// Registry: name → { positions, kind:'bucket'|'cohort', fn } — the single extension point.
export const FACTOR_RECONSTRUCTORS = { momentum:{…}, regression:{…}, trajectory:{…}, shareTrend:{…}, snapShare:{…}, rzUsage:{…}, teamRzShare:{…} };

// App-faithful Step-1 anchor: last-3 qualifying (gp≥8) under a PER-LENGTH weight table
// {3:[0.20,0.30,0.50], 2:[0.30,0.70], 1:[1.00]} (seasonProjection.js:317-319) — NOT a
// renormalization of the 3-vector (that would give [0.4,0.6] at two seasons). §0.3 item 19.
export function reconstructBasePPG(qualifyingSeasons) → number | null
```

**Bit-parity note for `reconstructBasePPG` (§0.3 item 31 — semantics unchanged).** The app divides the per-length weights by their own sum before use (`weights = weightsRaw.map(w => w / wSum)`, `seasonProjection.js:321-322`). That is an exact no-op at 3 seasons (`0.2+0.3+0.5 === 1`) and at 1, but **not** at 2: `0.3 + 0.7 === 0.9999999999999999` in IEEE754, so the applied weights are `[0.30000000000000004, 0.7000000000000001]`. Replicate the division **literally** rather than hard-coding normalized constants — the difference is ~1e-16 relative, immaterial except exactly at a 1dp rounding boundary, which is precisely where T-F10's exact-at-stored-precision gate (§9) would otherwise produce a spurious failure. Reduce in the same order (`recent.reduce((acc, s, i) => acc + s.ppg * weights[i], 0)`).

Mirror the constants and branches from: `momentum.js:18-35`; `regressionSignals.js:48-78`; `teamContext.js:314-348` (`computeShareTrend`) + `:269-308` (`computeHistoricalShares`) + `:240-260` (`computeHistoricalTeamTotals`) + `:18-21` (`resolveAttributedTeam`); `usageMetrics.js:40-179` (incl. the pool builder `:71-104`); `teamRzShare.js:31-169` (incl. the cohort builder `:68-99`); `seasonProjection.js:283-304, 315-323, 340-361, 363-384, 386-394, 461-465, 471-479, 481-497`.

### 3.2 The reconstruction pass — two seasons, one pool, sentinels not drops

`attachFactorMultipliers(rows, { totalsByYear, teamTotalsByYear, ppgByYear, fromYear, toYear })` — **pure, in `lib/panel.mjs`**; called from `assemblePanel` behind `withFactorMultipliers` (§6.3).

**Two distinct seasons — do not conflate:**
| Quantity | Season | App anchor |
|---|---|---|
| **Cohort pool** (percentile reference population) | **season Y** (`predictorYear`) | app's `refSeason = Math.max(seasons)` (`usageMetrics.js:72`, `teamRzShare.js:69`) |
| **Player's own counts + team denominator** | **`lastQ.season`** (most-recent gp≥8 qualifying ≤ Y) | `lastSeasonRaw = careerStats[lastQ.season][pid]` (`seasonProjection.js:407-408`), consumed at `:479` and `:488-491` |

They coincide when gp(Y) ≥ 8; they diverge exactly for rows with gp(Y) ∈ {6,7} (panel gate gp≥6, `lib/panel.mjs:235-236`) plus an earlier qualifying season. This is the app's real quirk — reproduce it, do not "fix" it. *(The share series is a third, separate span: **all** seasons `[HISTORY_FLOOR..Y]`, §3.4. T-F10's parity check runs at the snapshot's own `refSeason = 2025`, outside the predictor range — §9.)*

**Steps:**
1. **Per row, build `qualifyingSeasons`** = every `s ∈ [HISTORY_FLOOR .. Y]` where `computeSeasonPoints(pid, ppgByYear[s])` (`lib/panel.mjs:89`) yields finite `ppg` and `gamesPlayed ≥ 8`, ascending `[{season, ppg, gamesPlayed}]`; set `row.lastQSeason`. *(The app additionally skips a season with non-finite `fantasyPoints`; a published v3 file cannot carry one — **certified inert with a counter**, §3.0-C6 / T-F18c. Do not add the test to the hot path; do count the violations.)* Apply **exclusion rule R1** (§3.0-A): drop on `length === 0` (`rookiePathNoQualifying`) or no season-totals appearance in any `s < Y` (`rookiePathYearsExpProxy`); flag debut-in-`Y−1` rows into the sensitivity cohort. (Built here, not in `buildPanelRow` — keeps E-0a/flip row shape byte-identical, §6.2.)
2. **Per `(position, Y)`, build cohort pools via the exported `buildCohortPools`** (§6.2 — named and exported precisely so T-F8 and the T-F10 gate call production code rather than a copy, §0.3 item 36) from **EVERY** player in `totalsByYear[Y]` (all pids; position via `resolvePosition`) under the app's own gates — never the outcome-conditioned survivors:
   - snap pool: `off_snp / tm_off_snp` where `off_snp ≥ 100 && tm_off_snp > 0` (`usageMetrics.js:89`) — **RB/WR/TE only**; QB's snap pool stays empty by construction (`:75`, `:86`)
   - rz pool: `rzOwn / opp` where `opp ≥ minOpp` — **QB 50** (`pass_att`) / RB 30 (`rush_att`) / WR·TE 20 (`rec_tgt`) (`usageMetrics.js:96`). **Build the QB pool** — QB `rzUsage` is HELD-IN-ARM, not omitted (§2, §0.3 item 48), and a held-in-arm factor still has to be *reconstructed* to enter both arms. **Numerator is `(stats[rzKey] ?? 0)`, never a skip** (`:96`): a pool member with `opp ≥ minOpp` and an absent RZ key contributes a real `0`
   - teamRz pool: `rzOwn / teamDenom` where `opp ≥ minOpp && teamDenom ≥ 20` (`teamRzShare.js:83/88`), using the entity-filtered `buildTeamTotalsForSeason` (`lib/panel.mjs:69-85`) at season Y under per-season-team attribution; skip members whose season `team` is null (mirrors `teamRzShare.js:86`)
   - sort ascending (`percentileRank` expects sorted).
3. **Per row, compute multipliers for every member of `F_p^full`** — including HELD-IN-ARM members, which are reconstructed exactly like fitted ones and simply never become candidates (§1, §2). Bucket factors from `qualifyingSeasons` ppgs (§3.0-B1/2/3); `shareTrend` from `reconstructShareSeries` (§3.4); cohort factors from `totalsByYear[row.lastQSeason][pid].stats` raw counts against the **season-Y pools**, with the teamRzShare denominator from `teamTotalsByYear[row.lastQSeason].totals[lastQTeam]`, `lastQTeam = totalsByYear[row.lastQSeason][pid].team` (per-season-team; **no current-team fallback — the §3.0-C1 residual; count `team == null` rows**). **QB rows compute `rzUsage`** off `pass_rz_att`/`pass_att` against the QB pool; they compute no `snapShare` (QB sentinel, §3.0-B5) and no `teamRzShare` (QB sentinel, §3.0-B7).
4. `row.anchorBasePPG = reconstructBasePPG(row.qualifyingSeasons)`; null → drop (consistent with R1).
4a. **Positivity drop, before any log is taken (§1, §0.3 item 55).** Drop the row when `outcomePPG ≤ 0` (reason `nonPositiveOutcome`) or `anchorBasePPG ≤ 0` (reason `nonPositiveAnchor`); count each. These are **real row drops**, listed alongside R1 and null-`anchorBasePPG` in step 6's drop inventory — not sentinels. The panel's own gates do not cover them: `buildPanelRow` tests `ppg == null` / `gamesPlayed < minOutcomeGames` / `!Number.isFinite(ppg)` (`lib/panel.mjs:246-250`) and **never positivity**, while `buildHalfPprOutcomes` coerces `rec.fantasyPoints ?? 0` (`scripts/grade-snapshot.mjs:74`). Expected 0 or near-0 at gp≥6 — asserted by **T-F19**, so §3.0's stop rule does not fire here.
5. Apply forward-mover neutralization (§3.6).
6. **Sentinels are computed 1.0s, never drops (§3.0-B).** Every condition in the §3.0-B table's "flat 1.0" column produces a multiplier of exactly 1.0 and the row **stays in the fit** — including a `lastQSeason` predating `off_snp` coverage (`snapShareFactor = 1.0`), `opp ≤ 0`, `denom < 20`, `opp < minOpp` for teamRzShare, empty cohort pools, and a share series with fewer than 2 entries. **Series-level drops (row 4-S) are never row drops.** **The only row drops are:** R1, null `anchorBasePPG`, the panel's own pre-existing gates, and — if the §3.0-C1 escalation triggers — `nullSeasonTeam`.
   **Record two per-position, per-factor counters — REPORTING ONLY:**
   - **`sentinelCounts[position][factor]`** — rows that took each *sentinel branch* from the §3.0-B table. Explains *why* a column is flat.
   - **`flatOneCounts[position][factor]`** — rows whose reconstructed multiplier is **exactly 1.0** (`|log fᵢ| < FIT_FLAT_ONE_EPS`), by **any** route: a sentinel; a `stable` share-trend label (`shareTrendRaw = 1.00`); a `regressionFactor` bucket of `1.00` (**`outlierRatio ∈ [0.85, 1.15]`** — `>1.35 → 0.88` is tested first (`seasonProjection.js:370`), then `>1.15 → 0.95` catches `(1.15, 1.35]` **before the `else`** (`:371`), so the flat region ends at 1.15; §0.3 items 51/63 — a route with **no** sentinel available at all); or **`teamRzShare`'s in-module 3dp rounding**, which sends any factor in `[0.9995, 1.0005)` to exactly `1.000` (`teamRzShare.js:166`, §0.3 item 56 — likewise no sentinel taken).
   Both counters cover **every member of `F_p^full`**, HELD-IN-ARM included — QB `rzUsage` is never a fit candidate but its flat-1.0 rate is still worth reading (§0.3 items 48, 52). Keyed per position so the verdict can print them without a second producer (§0.3 item 40). **Neither counter is the decision**: rule 0b's pin is computed by `selectFitFactors` over `FIT_CANDIDATES[position]` on the position's fit rows (§4). Over that same row set the flat-1.0 numbers coincide with `flatOneCounts` by construction; the **single authority for the reported rate of a candidate is `selectFitFactors`' `flatOneRates`**, `flatOneCounts` is the only source for held-in-arm factors, and `sentinelCounts` is the diagnostic printed beside both.

> **Do not conflate with the E-0a feature of the same name:** the panel's existing `features.snapShare` is a season-Y *raw feature* for E-0a's linear grading; the fit's `multipliers.snapShare` is the reconstructed **app multiplier** at `lastQSeason`. Likewise `features.shareTrend` is a Y-vs-Y−1 *difference of two `computeShare` values* (`lib/panel.mjs:268-271`), while `multipliers.shareTrend` is the app's bucket×volatility multiplier over the §3.4 series. Different quantities; the fit uses only the latter.

### 3.3 History window — load to the 2012 floor
Multi-season factors use the app's **full qualifying history**: basePPG = last-3 of unbounded `qualifying` (`:315-323`), momentum ≥4, trajectory ≥2, consistency ≥3, shareTrend series + volatility over the whole series. The stock panel loads only `[fromYear−2 .. toYear+1]` (`panel-run.mjs:105-108`), truncating that history and silently returning neutral factors where the app returns real ones — a systematic bias in a no-intercept fit.

**Fix:** under `--fit`, load season-totals/outcome maps from **`HISTORY_FLOOR = 2012`** through `toYear+1`; advstats/roster stay `[fromYear..toYear]`. `assemblePanelRows` bounds its predictor loop to `[fromYear..toYear]` (`lib/panel.mjs:332`) independently of the load window, so widening the load adds history **without** creating spurious rows.
- **Verified (source + basis, one chain):** the app's projection `careerStats` comes from `loadCareerHistory` (`src/api/sleeperStats.js:237-267`), which loops `s = 2012 … currentSeason − 1` (`:240`) and, per season, returns the **data-store file verbatim** (`:145-159`) with a live-API aggregation fallback (`:161-228`). Two consequences: the 2012 load is **exact-match parity**, and the stored `fantasyPoints` the app divides by `gamesPlayed` is **half-PPR** (§3.0-C3) — which is why the fit runs `--basis half_ppr`.
- **Measure the residual as a diagnostic:** count rows whose earliest qualifying season **== 2012** and report per position. Because the app truncates identically, this is *not* a fidelity divergence.

### 3.4 shareSeries reconstruction — mirror `computeHistoricalShares`, not `computeShare`

`shareTrendMultiplier` consumes a multi-season series that the app builds in a **separate upstream function**. Reconstruct `computeHistoricalShares` (`teamContext.js:269-308`) semantics exactly — **do not reuse `computeShare` (`lib/panel.mjs:155-168`), whose panel semantics differ in four load-bearing ways** (§0.3 item 21). Implement as `reconstructShareSeries` (§3.1).

**Position:** use **the row's position, resolved once at Y** (`resolvePosition`, `lib/panel.mjs:98-106`), for **every** season of the series — mirroring the app, which reads one `playersMap[pid].position` (`:279`) and applies it to all seasons. Do not re-resolve per season. (Second consumption point of the §3.0-C2 divergence; no extra tolerance.)

**Per season `s ∈ [HISTORY_FLOOR .. Y]`, ascending — emit an entry only if every condition holds:**
1. **`gamesPlayed ≥ 8`** for `totalsByYear[s][pid]` (`:276`). A gp 1–7 part-season is **absent from the series**, not a low share.
2. Position ∈ {RB, WR, TE} (`:280`) — QB never has a series.
3. `team = totalsByYear[s][pid].team` (per-season-team; **no current-team fallback** — §3.0-C1) is non-null (`:282`), and a team-totals entry exists for `(s, team)` (`:284`).
4. **Own volume must be positive, else the season is dropped** (`:300`) — never a 0:
   - **RB:** `rush_att > 0` (`:290`) → `share = rush_att / Math.max(teamTotals.rushAtt, 1)`.
   - **WR/TE:** if `rec_tgt > 0` **and** `teamTotals.recTgt > 0` (`:293`) → `share = rec_tgt / Math.max(teamTotals.recTgt, 1)` (`:294`); **else fallback** — if `rec > 0` (`:297`; the `rec` read is `:296`) → `share = rec / Math.max(teamTotals.rec, 1)` (`:297`); **else no entry**.
5. **No `TEAM_DENOM_MIN` floor anywhere in this step** — the app's only guard is `Math.max(denom, 1)`. (The 20-floor belongs to `teamRzShare`, §3.0-B7, and to the panel's own `computeShare` at `lib/panel.mjs:164/167` — which is why that function is not reused.) A sub-20 team denominator still yields an entry; count how often and report.
6. Drop non-finite shares (`:300`). A `share > 1` is kept (the app only warns, `:301`) — count it: post-fix it signals an entity-filter/attribution violation and should be ~0.
7. **Round to 3dp before storing** — `Math.round(share*1000)/1000` (`:304`). Trend and volatility are computed on the **rounded** values.

**Denominators for step 4** come from the same per-year `buildTeamTotalsForSeason` build used by §3.2 (entity-filtered since `0396050`, per-season-team), extended with the additive `rec` accumulator (§6.2) so the WR/TE fallback is reproducible. The app-side `gamesPlayed ≥ 1` contributor gate is **certified inert with an assertion** (§3.0-C4, T-F18b).

**Then the transform** (`computeShareTrend`, `teamContext.js:314-348`), on the series above:
1. `<2 entries → multiplier 1.0` (`:315`; §3.0-B4).
2. `recentShare` = last entry's share (`:317`).
3. **`priorShare` = weighted mean of up to the 3 most-recent PRIOR seasons** at 50/30/20, each weight counted only if that season exists, divided by `totalW` (`:320-328`) — **not** the whole series.
4. `trend = (recentShare − priorShare) / Math.max(priorShare, 0.01)` (`:330`); labels `:332-337` {>0.20 growing, >0.05 expanding, ≥−0.05 stable, ≥−0.20 shrinking, else declining}.
5. `shareVolatility` = **sample SD (n−1)** over the **whole** series (`:341-343`); labels `:344-346` {`<0.05` entrenched, `≤0.10` moderate, else volatile}.
6. Multiplier = `1 + (labelMultiplier − 1) × volatilityScale` (`seasonProjection.js:342-361`); `isTeamChange === true → 1.0` (§3.6). **Note for rule 0b:** the `stable` label gives `shareTrendRaw = 1.00` ⇒ multiplier exactly 1.0 with **no sentinel taken** — one of the flat-1.0 routes `flatOneCounts` exists to surface (§3.2 step 6).

**Coverage to record** (into `fitCoverage`, reported in the verdict): per position, series length distribution; per-reason series drops (`belowGp8`, `nullTeam`, `noTeamEntry`, `zeroOwnVolume`, `nonFinite`); `recFallbackUsed`; `subMinDenomKept`; `shareGtOne`.

This widens the team-totals build from the current Y/Y−1 pair (`lib/panel.mjs:343-345`) to per-loaded-year (bounded, ≤14 seasons); the same per-year totals feed §3.2's teamRz pool and denominators (see §6.3).

### 3.5 Parity guards — three tiers, honestly scoped
- **T-F5 golden fixtures (unit):** each `reconstruct*` returns the exact app-documented multiplier, including each §3.0-B sentinel branch. Mirror-contract tripwire (§11).
- **T-F17 series-construction parity (unit):** `reconstructShareSeries` reproduces every 4-S branch (§9).
- **T-F10 real-player snapshot parity (integration) — app ground truth, 5 of 7 factors:** reconstruct the snapshot's **veteran-path** players **on the app's own half-PPR basis**, through the **same exported builders the production path uses** (`buildCohortPools`, `FACTOR_RECONSTRUCTORS`), and assert agreement on `momentum`, `regression`, `trajectory`, `snapShare`, `rzUsage`.
- **T-F11 synthetic denominator isolation (unit):** proves the entity filter is the sole cause of the ½-scale share, on constructed fixtures. *(Now also a regression guard on the landed `0396050` filter.)*
- **Gap:** `shareTrend` and `teamRzShare` have **no** end-to-end app-ground-truth check until a post-2026-07-18 snapshot exists (R0-BANK); then extend T-F10. *Rejected alternative:* parity-checking `shareTrendRaw` via scale-invariance of the trend ratio — the 3dp rounding applied **before** the trend (§3.4 step 7) breaks that invariance. Do not adopt.

### 3.6 Forward-mover neutralization
The app forces `shareTrendMultiplier→1.0` **and** `teamRzShareFactor→1.0` on `isTeamChange === true` (`:359-361`, `:493-497`); it does **not** neutralize the other five. The retrospective proxy is `forwardMover = team(Y) ≠ team(Y+1)` from the existing **`classifyAttributionCohort`** (`lib/panel.mjs:642`, forwardMover at `:662-663`, already used by the flip gate — reuse, don't fork; build the lite `teamsByYear` from the already-loaded `totalsByYear`, which spans `toYear+1`). Set both to 1.0 for those rows; **keep the row**. Caveat: `forwardMover` uses realized team(Y+1) while the app uses the offseason-known new team — they agree for the large majority; the residual is the same retrospective-labeling caveat the flip gate carries.

---

## 4. The fit + comparison + verdict (in `lib/panel.mjs`)

```js
// Identifiability selection — ONE call per position, over that position's full fit-row set,
// ranging over FIT_CANDIDATES[position] (NOT F_p^full — held-in-arm factors are never
// candidates, §1/§2). Pure; α-independent and fold-independent. The returned fitFactors
// are FIXED for every downstream fit (§0.3 item 39).
export function selectFitFactors(rows, position, { maxFlatOneRate = FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE, eps = FIT_FLAT_ONE_EPS } = {})
  → { fitFactors:[…names],          // F_p^fit — estimated
      pinned:[…names],              // candidates removed by rule 0b (data)
      heldInArm:[…names],           // FULL_FACTORS[p] \ FIT_CANDIDATES[p] (config) — echoed so the
                                    //   verdict writer has one source for the full disposition split
      flatOneRates:{[name]:number}, // EVERY candidate, pinned or not (§0.3 item 52)
      n:number }

// Receives the fixed estimated set — it does not decide or return a pin.
// `w` carries an entry for every factor in F_p^full; pinned, held-in-arm and
// fold-neutralized entries are exactly 1.
export function fitExponents(trainRows, position, { alpha, fitFactors })
  → { w:{[name]:number}, scales:{[name]:number},
      estimatedFactors:[…names],    // fitFactors minus `neutralized` — the support actually fit on THESE rows
      neutralized:[{ factor, reason:'flatOnTrain'|'nonFiniteScale', flatRate, s }],  // §0.3 items 47/57
      maxAbsWMinus1:number,         // max |w_i − 1| over estimated factors — explosion tripwire (§7)
      meanLogResidual:number, nTrain:number, singular:boolean }

// Also receives the fixed set — which is what mechanically prevents the α-sweep
// from re-selecting (§0.3 item 40). CV SCORER ONLY: it does not produce wFinal
// (gradeExponentFit owns the all-rows shipped refit — §0.3 item 59).
export function evaluateExponentModel(rows, folds, position, { alpha, fitFactors })
  → { fitted:{pooled:{n,mae,spearmanMean}, perEvalYear:[…], predictions:[…]}, hand:{…},
      wByFold:[{ evalYear, w, scales, estimatedFactors, neutralized, maxAbsWMinus1 }],
      clampHits:{ fitted:number, hand:number },   // inner [0.67,1.50] envelope hits, per arm (§0.3 item 54)
      meanLogResidual:number }

export function gradeExponentFit(rows, folds, position, { alpha, alphaSweep })
  → { position,
      nFitRows,                     // this position's full fit-row count — REPORTED, never gating
      nEvalRows,                    // rows whose predictorYear is some fold's evalYear — the GATE's numerator
      fitFactorsFull, fitFactorsEstimated, pinnedFactors, heldInArmFactors,
      flatOneRates, params:|F_p^fit|, nToParam, fitted, hand,
      deltas:{ maePooled, maePerYear:[{evalYear,dMae}], spearmanMean },
      wFinal, wByAlpha:{[α]:wFinal}, sweep:[{alpha,dMae,dSpearman}], meanLogResidual,
      foldNeutralization:{ [factor]: { folds:number, reasons:{ flatOnTrain:number, nonFiniteScale:number } } },
      maxAbsWMinus1ByFold:[…numbers],
      clampHits:{ fitted:number, hand:number },
      shippedRefitNeutralized:[…],  // expect [] — non-empty is a hard stop, §4 step 5
      verdict }                     // ∈ FIT_VERDICT_LABELS; INSUFFICIENT-POWER short-circuits at step 3

// BASE label only. Never sees an under-powered position (gradeExponentFit short-circuits
// before calling it) and never sees the sensitivity re-run (runFit owns that override,
// §6.3) — so nToParam and a sensitivity label are both absent by design (§0.3 item 49).
export function decideFitVerdict({ deltas, sweep, handMae, wByAlpha }, position)
  → 'CLEARS'|'NO-GAIN'|'DEGRADES'|'UNSTABLE'

export const FIT_VERDICT_LABELS = ['CLEARS','NO-GAIN','DEGRADES','UNSTABLE','INSUFFICIENT-POWER'];
```
**One producer per key (§0.3 items 40, 59).** `flatOneRates`/`pinned`/`heldInArm` come from `selectFitFactors`. `scales`, `estimatedFactors`, `neutralized` and `maxAbsWMinus1` live on `fitExponents`' return and are surfaced through `wByFold` entries. `foldNeutralization`, `maxAbsWMinus1ByFold` and the position-level `clampHits` are `gradeExponentFit`'s aggregations. **`wFinal` and `shippedRefitNeutralized` have exactly one producer — `gradeExponentFit`** (§4 step 5), via a direct `fitExponents` call over all `posRows`; `evaluateExponentModel` **does not return `wFinal`**: it is the CV scorer and owns per-fold results only. **No per-position `sentinelRates` is returned** — sentinel counts are produced by `attachFactorMultipliers` into `fitCoverage` (§3.2 step 6) and read from there by the verdict writer.

**Verdict is produced on two channels, and only two (§0.3 item 49):**
| Label | Produced by | How |
|---|---|---|
| `INSUFFICIENT-POWER` | `gradeExponentFit` | rule 0 short-circuits at step 3, before any fit; `decideFitVerdict` is never called |
| `CLEARS` / `NO-GAIN` / `DEGRADES` / `UNSTABLE` | `decideFitVerdict` | rules 1–4 on ΔMAE / ΔSpearman / α-stability |
| `UNSTABLE` **override** | `runFit` (§6.3) | base label ≠ sensitivity-run label → `UNSTABLE`, per §3.0-A |

**Shrinkage knob:** dimensionless `α` (ridge = `α·nTrain` after RMS scaling). Shipped **`α = 0.5`**; sweep **`{0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2}`**.

#### Rule 0b — the identifiability guard (one selection per position)

**The quantity.** `flatOneRate(i, rows)` = fraction of `rows` whose reconstructed multiplier for factor `i` is exactly 1.0 (`|log fᵢ(r)| < FIT_FLAT_ONE_EPS`), **by any route** — sentinel branch, `stable` share-trend label, or a `regressionFactor` bucket of 1.00 — that is, `outlierRatio` in **[0.85, 1.15]** — `>1.35 → 0.88` is tested **first** (`seasonProjection.js:370`), then `>1.15 → 0.95` catches `(1.15, 1.35]` **before the `else`** (`:371`), so the flat region ends at **1.15, not 1.35** (§0.3 items 51/63). Plus **`teamRzShare`'s in-module 3dp rounding**, which sends `[0.9995, 1.0005)` to exactly `1.000` (`teamRzShare.js:166`, §0.3 item 56). Neither of those last two routes takes a sentinel at all; gating on sentinel hits alone would miss exactly those columns (§0.3 item 29).

**Where it is computed, and why once.** `flatOneRate` is a **function of the design matrix only — it never reads `outcomePPG`** — so computing it over the position's full fit-row set leaks nothing about the target and cannot inflate ΔMAE. (Compare the quantities that *are* outcome-derived and stay strictly train-local: `standardizeTrainApply`'s `outcomeMean`/`outcomeSd`, `lib/panel.mjs:438-442`, consumed at `:447`.) Selecting once and fixing the set gives a property per-fold selection cannot: **the shipped refit and every scored fold draw from an identical factor support** — same estimated set, same pinned set. That is **support-identity, not vector-identity**; `wFinal` is an all-rows refit no fold scored out of sample (§0.2, §8 item 1, §0.3 items 39/50).

**The rule.** `selectFitFactors(posRows, position)` ranges over `FIT_CANDIDATES[position]`, pins every candidate with `flatOneRate ≥ FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE (0.90)`, and returns the rest as `fitFactors`. **One selection rule, no second policy** — and the degenerate-scale case is handled as *degradation*, not as a second gate:

**Degenerate scale degrades gracefully, per fold — triggered on a RATE, not on exact zero (§0.3 items 47, 57).** On any fold where a retained factor trips the trigger below on that fold's **train** rows, **neutralize that factor for that fold** — fix its exponent at 1, exclude its column from that fold's design matrix, push `{factor, reason, flatRate, s}` onto `neutralized`, and **continue the run**. Never abort.

*Why this is reachable and an abort would have been wrong.* `selectFitFactors` runs **once globally** over `posRows`; `s_i` is an **RMS scale computed per fold on train rows** (§1 step 2). A factor whose global flat-1.0 rate sits below 0.90 — retained — can be far flatter on **one fold's train subset**, since a fold's train set is a proper subset of years. A throw would abort the whole `--fit` run over one thin fold. Item 34's redundancy argument (`s_i === 0 ⟺ flatOneRate === 1.0`, already pinned) is true **only at the scope the selection saw**; it does not transfer to a train subset. T-F3(d)'s former "unreachable for retained factors" rationale was false (§9).

*Why the trigger is a rate and not `s_i === 0` (§0.3 item 57 — this tightens the existing predicate, it does not add a guard).* Exact-zero catches only the **fully** flat fold. The same global-vs-fold mismatch also produces the **near**-degenerate fold — say 99% flat on train — and there `s_i > 0` passes, so the old trigger stayed silent. That case is the dangerous one:
- **RMS scaling does not protect it.** The scaled Gram diagonal is `nTrain` **regardless of `s_i`** (§1 step 2), so ridge shrinkage on `β` is unchanged as `s_i → 0`.
- **The mapping back explodes.** `δ_i = β_i / s_i` (§1 step 4) diverges as `s_i → 0`.
- **§1 step 4's bound does not apply.** Its reassurance — effect stays bounded because `δ·log f` has tiny `log f` — assumes the **eval** rows are flat too. Here they are not: the factor is flat on *train* and live on *eval*, which is exactly the configuration that puts an exploded exponent onto rows that move.

**The trigger:** neutralize factor `i` on a fold when its flat-1.0 rate over that fold's **train rows** is `≥ FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE` (0.90). Same constant, same statistic, same pin-not-drop semantics as rule 0b — **only the row set differs** (fold-train vs position-wide). That is why this is one rule evaluated at two scopes, not a second policy.

*Two reasons, recorded separately, because they mean different things:*
- **`flatOnTrain`** (train-row flat-1.0 rate ≥ 0.90, `s_i` small or zero) — expected, benign, a property of a thin fold. Report the rate; it does not impugn the run.
- **`nonFiniteScale`** (`s_i` non-finite) — only reachable if a reconstructed multiplier is exactly 0 or ∞, which every app clamp forbids (`usageMetrics.js:152`, `:173`; `teamRzShare.js:162`; `seasonProjection.js:465`; bucket×dampener forms bottom out at 0.88/0.92 via `:342-361`, `:369-384`, `:388-394`). This is a **reconstruction-fidelity failure**, not a degeneracy. The run still completes — but it joins §7's expect-0 assertion set beside `zeroGpWithStats` and `nonFiniteFantasyPoints`, so it surfaces in the fidelity block rather than being laundered into a benign counter. Investigate before trusting the verdict.

*Belt and suspenders, kept:* **`Number.isFinite(s_i) && s_i > 0`** remains as an assertion **behind** the rate trigger, for any factor that survives it. A multiplier of exactly 0 gives `log f = −Infinity ⇒ s_i = Infinity`, which passes `> 0` and then feeds `x'_i = −Inf/Inf = NaN` into `solveOLS` — where the pivot test `maxVal < 1e-10` is `false` for `NaN` and returns `singular: false` silently (`lib/backtest.mjs:63`). Failing it routes to `nonFiniteScale`, never to a throw.

*Residual explosion tripwire:* report per-fold **`max|w_i − 1|`** over estimated factors (`maxAbsWMinus1`, surfaced as `maxAbsWMinus1ByFold` in §7). A fold that slips past both the rate trigger and the finiteness assertion but produces an outsized exponent is then visible in the verdict rather than silently priced into ΔMAE.

*Where it cannot fire:* the shipped all-rows refit (step 5 below). There a train-row flat rate ≥ 0.90 **is** the position-wide flat rate, so `selectFitFactors` already pinned the factor — item 34's collapse holds at that scope. So `shippedRefitNeutralized` must come back empty; a non-empty value is a **hard stop-and-investigate**, not a degradation.

**Order of operations in `gradeExponentFit`:**
1. `posRows` = this position's fit rows.
2. `sel = selectFitFactors(posRows, position)` — **once**, over `FIT_CANDIDATES[position]`. `F_p^fit = sel.fitFactors` is fixed from here.
3. **Power gate (rule 0)** on `nEvalRows / |sel.fitFactors|`. `nEvalRows` = rows whose `predictorYear` is some fold's `evalYear` — computable from `rows` + `folds` **without fitting**, so the gate still runs here, before the α loop (§0.3 item 60). If it trips, **return immediately with `verdict = 'INSUFFICIENT-POWER'`** — no fit, no α loop, and `decideFitVerdict` is never called (§0.3 item 49).
4. For each α in `{shipped} ∪ alphaSweep`: `evaluateExponentModel(posRows, folds, position, { alpha, fitFactors: sel.fitFactors })` — per fold, `trainRows = rows.filter(r => trainYears.includes(r.predictorYear))` exactly as `evaluateModel:487-489` does; RMS scales and coefficients are train-only; eval rows are scored with that fold's `w`. Fold-level graceful neutralization is recorded per fold and aggregated into `foldNeutralization`.
5. Shipped refit at `α = 0.5` over all `posRows` with the same `fitFactors` — **a direct `fitExponents` call owned by `gradeExponentFit`, the single producer of `wFinal`** (§0.3 item 59; `evaluateExponentModel` returns no `wFinal`). The all-rows-refit precedent is `fitDescriptive` (`lib/panel.mjs:529-536`, "Final descriptive fit on all rows (no holdout) — reported coefficients only, not scored"). Capture that call's `neutralized` as `shippedRefitNeutralized`; **expect `[]`**.
6. `verdict = decideFitVerdict({ deltas, sweep, handMae, wByAlpha }, position)` — the **base** label. The sensitivity override is applied later, by `runFit` (§6.3), not here.

**Pin, do not remove from the product.** A pinned factor's `wᵢ` is **1** and it stays in **both** `predHand` and `predFitted` (§1), so the hand baseline remains the app's true hand-tuned prediction. The same holds for a HELD-IN-ARM factor (QB `rzUsage`) and for a fold-level neutralization — in every case the term is identical in both arms and cancels in that fold's `ΔMAE`, which is exactly why neutralizing is safe rather than merely convenient. *Accepted tradeoff:* a factor informative only on a <10% tail is pinned rather than estimated from that tail — nothing is lost from the baseline, and a noisy exponent is not bought with 10% of the rows.

**Verdict (ordered rules — mirror `decideVerdict:607`; goalposts fixed):**
**Rule 0 is `gradeExponentFit`'s (step 3 above); rules 1–4 are `decideFitVerdict`'s; the sensitivity override is `runFit`'s (§6.3).** Keeping them on separate channels is what makes each function's signature honest (§0.3 item 49).

0. **INSUFFICIENT-POWER (deferral default)** — **`nToParam = nEvalRows / |F_p^fit| < 20`** → **do not fit**; return the label **`INSUFFICIENT-POWER`** (a first-class member of `FIT_VERDICT_LABELS`, not a `NO-GAIN` carrying a reason string; it keeps hand-tuned exactly as `NO-GAIN` does). Effective n is below pooled n (recurring Y→Y+1 players); the floor is deliberately conservative.
   **The numerator is pooled EVAL n — the basis the threshold was calibrated on (§0.3 item 60).** §5's `n:p` column is eval n (WR 339/7 ≈ 48; RB ~28; TE ~23; QB ~31). Fit rows span all five predictor years while eval rows span three, so substituting `nFitRows` would inflate `n:p` by ≈1.67× and **loosen the gate exactly where it guards hardest** — QB ~31 → ~52, TE ~23 → ~38, i.e. the two positions the deferral exists for would both stop tripping it. It is also the principled basis: the gate asks whether the **verdict** has power, and the verdict's evidence is the out-of-sample eval rows. `nFitRows` is defined and reported beside it, but **never gates**.
1. `DEGRADES` — pooled ΔMAE (fitted − hand) > 0.
2. `CLEARS` — pooled ΔMAE < 0 AND mean ΔSpearman ≥ 0 AND ΔMAE < 0 in ≥ 2 of 3 eval years AND ΔMAE sign stable across `α∈{0.25,0.5,1}` AND (**thin-position guard**) `sign(wFinal_i − 1)` agrees between `α=0.5` and `α=2` for every **estimated** factor (mandatory QB/TE, applied to all).
3. `NO-GAIN` — `|pooled ΔMAE| / handMae < 0.005`.
4. `UNSTABLE` — everything else.

**Then, in `runFit` (§6.3) — the sensitivity override (§3.0-A).** Each position is graded twice: once on all fit rows, once excluding the debut-in-`Y−1` cohort. The second run is a **full independent re-run** — its own `selectFitFactors`, its own folds — so its `F_p^fit` may differ; that difference is itself reportable, and because it changes the parameterization a label difference is exactly what the override is for. If `baseVerdict ≠ sensitivityVerdict`, the position's final `verdict` is **`UNSTABLE`**. Never pick the favourable run. Run the sensitivity pass unconditionally, including when the base label is `INSUFFICIENT-POWER`: the reduced row set has fewer rows **but possibly a smaller `|F_p^fit|`**, so a lower `nToParam` is not guaranteed and must not be assumed.

**Shipped vector = `wFinal` at α=0.5, CLEARS positions only** — including the pinned `wᵢ = 1` entries, so the activation unit receives an unambiguous full-length vector. Otherwise the app keeps hand-tuned (`wᵢ=1` everywhere). Self-protecting: a thin/noisy panel does not clear.

**WR+TE pool fallback (assessment §B.4):** also fit a pooled WR+TE vector (cohorts stay position-separate; one selection over the pooled row set). If TE alone is UNSTABLE/NO-GAIN/INSUFFICIENT-POWER but the pool CLEARS, report the pooled vector as TE's shippable alternative. WR always uses its own.
