## 5. Panel size per position — the binding constraint

**Read from the baseline of record, `grading/2026-08-08-e0a-verdict.md`** (predictor 2020–2024; CV warm-up 2 seasons → eval years 2022/2023/2024 via `forwardChainFolds(years, 2)`, `lib/panel.mjs:399-409`; that verdict runs `attribution=current-team`, `basis=custom`):

| Pos | Pooled eval n (2026-08-08 baseline) | Baseline MAE | Fit params | n : p | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WR | **339** | 2.690 | 7 | ~48 | Comfortable (rows non-independent across Y→Y+1) |
| RB | **197** | 3.274 | 7 | ~28 | Adequate |
| TE | **164** | 2.376 | 7 | ~23 | **Marginal** — α-stability guard + WR+TE pool |
| QB | **92** | 3.631 | 3 *(4 in the product — `rzUsage` HELD-IN-ARM)* | ~31 | **Underpowered** — 3 eval years, heavy non-independence; expect NO-GAIN |

**Fit params = `|F_p^fit|`, not `|F_p^full|`.** QB's product carries **four** factors but only **three** are estimable, so its `n:p` is computed on 3 and is unchanged by §0.3 item 48. The fourth costs no degrees of freedom — it is fixed at `wᵢ = 1` in both arms.

**This `n:p` column is the deferral gate's basis (§0.3 item 60).** The numbers above are **pooled eval n ÷ `|F_p^fit|`**, and §4 rule 0's `nToParam` is computed the same way (`nEvalRows / |F_p^fit|`), so the table and the gate cannot drift apart. `nFitRows` — the position's full fit-row count across all five predictor years, ≈1.67× larger — is reported beside it and **never gates**.

**The entity-filter fix did not move row survival** — pooled eval n is identical to the superseded 2026-07-08 verdict (WR 339 / RB 197 / TE 164 / QB 92); only feature *values* and therefore baseline MAE moved (RB 3.258→3.274, WR 2.693→2.690, TE 2.384→2.376, QB unchanged). The earlier prediction that a "handful" of rows might cross the `TEAM_DENOM_MIN` floor did not materialize.

These are still **not** the fit's row counts. They will move for reasons unrelated to the fix: **R1 rookie-path exclusion (§3.0-A) removes rows this table counts**, the fit runs `per-season-team` + `half_ppr` (both differ from the baseline verdict's configuration), and rule 0b can shrink `|F_p^fit|` (raising `n:p`). §12 step 1 re-reads actual coverage from the fit's own panel; the power/deferral decision uses **post-R1, fit-configuration** numbers.

**Recommendation: shrink harder toward the prior; do not fit noise.** Levers: the ridge-toward-`w=1` prior (§1); `α=0.5` with thin positions leaning larger; the **`n:p<20` deferral** and the **identifiability guard** (§4 rules 0/0b); the **α-stability guard**; the **WR+TE pool**. **Expected: WR most likely CLEARS; RB plausible; TE marginal (lean on the pool); QB most likely NO-GAIN — the gate working, not a failure.**

**R1-SNAPS tension (surface, don't ignore).** `roadmap.md` R3-FIT lists **R1-SNAPS (panel width, precondition a)**, still **open** — `PANEL_DEFAULTS.fromYear` is pinned 2020 with the comment "flip fromYear→2013 post-R1-SNAPS" (`lib/panel.mjs:15`). The harness is **panel-width-agnostic**: after R1-SNAPS the identical fit re-runs on 2013+ (config only: `--from 2013` + the `loadSnapShare` swap, `panel-run.mjs:52`), ~tripling every n. So **run now** with the self-protecting gate, **re-run unchanged** when the panel widens. The verdict states today's panel is the narrow pre-R1-SNAPS window.

**Reduced-pipeline caveat (state in the verdict):** the gate compares fitted-`w` vs hand-`w` on the **reduced reconstructable pipeline**; **HELD-OMITTED** factors (age, depth, team, qbQuality, efficiency, comp) are out of BOTH arms — the same limitation E-0a carries. A reduced-pipeline CLEARS is the pre-registered pre-2027 activation criterion (roadmap **D-1**); it is **provisional**, re-validated by R4 forward grading (assessment E-3c).

**QB held list — three groups, and the structural set is THREE factors, not two (§2 legend, §0.3 items 48, 62).** The verdict prints this enumeration verbatim, so it has to be right:

1. **HELD-OMITTED** — the list above (age, depth, team, qbQuality, efficiency, comp, bounceBack, tdReliance, breakout). Out of **both** arms. This is the reduced-pipeline limitation.
2. **Structural sentinels — `shareTrend`, `snapShare`, `teamRzShare` (three).** All three are neutralized **by the app itself** for QB, so their absence from `F_QB^full` is *fidelity*, not reduction: `snapShare` — QB ∉ `SNAP_POSITIONS` (§3.0-B5); `teamRzShare` — `RZ_SHARE_CONFIG` has no QB entry (§3.0-B7); **`shareTrend`** — `computeHistoricalShares` skips any position ∉ {RB,WR,TE} (`teamContext.js:280`), so a QB has no series, `computeShareTrend(null)` returns `null` (`:315`) at the call site (`seasonProjection.js:341`), and the multiplier is structurally `1.0`. *(This third one was missing from the prior revision's "two structural sentinels" wording.)*
3. **HELD-IN-ARM — `rzUsageFactor` (one).** **Not** a reduced-pipeline omission and **not** structural: the app really applies it to QB, so it is reconstructed and present in **both** QB arms at `wᵢ = 1`. That is the whole point — had it been dropped from the arms instead, QB's hand baseline would have been missing a multiplier the app applies, and the QB verdict would have compared the fitted stack against a baseline that is not the app's, apples to oranges.

⇒ **`F_QB^full` = `{momentum, regression, trajectory, rzUsage}`** (4), **`FIT_CANDIDATES.QB` = `{momentum, regression, trajectory}`** (3). Group 2 is excluded from `F_QB^full` because the app zeroes it out; group 3 is included because the app does not. Print the three groups separately in the verdict, never merged into one "held" bullet.

## 6. Edits, grouped by file

### 6.1 `lib/projectionFactors.mjs` (NEW — pure, no I/O) — §3
Reconstruction registry + the seven `reconstruct*` + `reconstructShareSeries` + `reconstructBasePPG` (with the §3.1 bit-parity note), each conforming to its §3.0-B row (transform rows **and** row 4-S). Header states the mirror contract (§11) and cites every app anchor mirrored, including the two upstream producers (`computeHistoricalShares`, `computeHistoricalTeamTotals`).

### 6.2 `lib/panel.mjs` (additive — **no change to any existing E-0a export or row shape**)
Anchors below are at HEAD `0396050` (§0.3 item 43).
- Constants: **`FULL_FACTORS`** (the product set — `{QB:['momentum','regression','trajectory','rzUsage'], RB:[…7], WR:[…7], TE:[…7]}`) and **`FIT_CANDIDATES`** (the estimable subset — QB drops `rzUsage`, everything else identical), both §2; **`ENVELOPE_FACTORS = ['momentum','trajectory','snapShare','rzUsage','teamRzShare']`** — the members of the app's `combinedNewFactorRaw` product (`seasonProjection.js:594-597`) that this pipeline reconstructs, used to partition the prediction into `inner`/`outer` (§1, §0.3 item 54); **`FIT_COMBINED_CLAMP = [0.67, 1.50]`** (`:598`) and the outer `[0, 40]` (`:601`); `FIT_VERDICT_LABELS` (§4); `HISTORY_FLOOR = 2012`, `FIT_ALPHA_DEFAULT = 0.5`, `FIT_ALPHA_SWEEP = [0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2]`, `FIT_MIN_N_TO_PARAM = 20`, `FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE = 0.90`, `FIT_FLAT_ONE_EPS = 1e-12`.
  **Three factor-set constants, not one `FIT_FACTORS`.** The product set, the candidate set and the envelope membership are three different questions — *what multiplies in*, *what may be estimated*, *what the app clamps together* — and each is orthogonal to the others (`shareTrend` is in the product and a candidate but **not** enveloped; `rzUsage` for QB is in the product and **is** enveloped but is **not** a candidate). Conflating the first two is what dropped QB `rzUsage` from the hand arm (§0.3 item 48); ignoring the third is what let the fitted arm skip the clamp (item 54). `FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE` is deliberately reused at **two scopes** — position-wide by `selectFitFactors`, fold-train by the neutralization trigger (§4, item 57) — one constant, one statistic.
- **`buildTeamTotalsForSeason` — one additive line (§3.0-C5).** The function already carries the `TEAM_*` entity filter (`:74`) and the `aggregateRowsExcluded` counter (`:72`, returned `:84`) from `0396050`. Add `rec` to the initializer (`:77`) and `totals[team].rec += s.rec || 0;` beside the existing four accumulators (`:79-82`), mirroring app `teamContext.js:252`. **Why safe:** (a) no existing consumer reads `.rec` — `computeShare` reads `rushAtt`/`recTgt` (`:163/:166`), `computeTeamRzShare` reads the RZ keys (`:195/:198`); (b) team totals are **never serialized** — `scripts/panel-run.mjs` contains no `teamTotals` reference; they live and die inside `assemblePanelRows`, so E-0a/flip artifacts are byte-identical; (c) the alternative — a fit-local parallel denominator builder — would fork denominator logic. No sequencing gate: the precondition is already in place.
- **`buildCohortPools(totalsSeason, positionOf, teamTotalsSeason)` — NEW export, pure (§0.3 item 36).** Returns `{ [position]: { snap:number[], rz:number[], teamRz:number[] } }`, each sorted ascending, built under the app's pool gates (§3.2 step 2). This is the code §3.2 step 2 already specifies, **named and exported instead of written inline**, so `attachFactorMultipliers`, T-F8 and the T-F10 gate all call *the same function*. `positionOf` is a `pid → position|null` callback (production passes a `resolvePosition` closure over that year's advstats/roster; T-F10 passes its fixture map), which is what keeps the gate free of loader wiring. `teamTotalsSeason` is one season's `buildTeamTotalsForSeason` result (`{ totals, unattributed, aggregateRowsExcluded }`) and is used only for the `teamRz` pool.
- **`selectFitFactors(rows, position, opts)` — NEW export, pure (§4).** The identifiability decision, called once per position over `FIT_CANDIDATES[position]`. Exported because it is the direct unit under test for rule 0b (T-F3). It also echoes `heldInArm` from config so the verdict writer has a single source for the full FIT / pinned / held-in-arm split (§0.3 item 52).
- **`attachFactorMultipliers(rows, ctx)`** (§3.2) — pure; builds `qualifyingSeasons`/`lastQSeason`, applies R1, calls `buildCohortPools`, builds the per-row share series (§3.4), computes `lastQ`-anchored multipliers with sentinels, `anchorBasePPG`, forward-mover neutralization (reusing `classifyAttributionCohort:642`); returns `{ rows, fitCoverage: { droppedByReason, sentinelCounts, flatOneCounts, seriesDrops, seriesLengths, recFallbackUsed, subMinDenomKept, shareGtOne, zeroGpWithStats, nonFiniteFantasyPoints, truncatedAt2012, forwardMoverNeutralized, nullSeasonTeam, debutYMinus1, nonPositiveOutcome, nonPositiveAnchor } }` — `sentinelCounts` and `flatOneCounts` keyed **per position** (§3.2 step 6); the two `nonPositive*` counters are the §3.2 step 4a drops (§0.3 item 55) and also appear inside `droppedByReason`.
- `fitExponents` / `evaluateExponentModel` / `gradeExponentFit` / `decideFitVerdict` (§4) — reuse `forwardChainFolds:399-409`, `solveOLS`/`spearman` (imported `:10`); mirror `evaluateModel:487-489`'s fold-row filtering exactly.
- **Untouched:** `buildPanelRow` (`:228-303` — the `qualifyingSeasons` edit is **withdrawn**), `computeShare` (`:155-168` — **explicitly not reused by the fit and not modified**, §3.4), `standardizeTrainApply` (`:417-452`), `fitAndScoreFold` (`:456`), `evaluateModel` (`:482`), `gradeCandidate` (`:543`), `fitDescriptive` (`:529-536`), `teamKeyResolver` (`:53-61`).

## 8. Activation handoff (name it, do NOT build it)

`r3fit-activation.md` (app repo, separate session) ships; this verdict is its authorization. State in the verdict + task summary:
1. **Ship only CLEARS positions'** `wFinal` (α=0.5) as per-position constants in `seasonProjection.js`; every other label keeps `wᵢ=1`. A **pinned** factor (rule 0b, data) and a **HELD-IN-ARM** factor (config — QB `rzUsage`) each ship as `wᵢ = 1`: part of the vector, not an omission. QB's vector is therefore length **4**, not 3.

   **What fixing `F_p^fit` before evaluation does and does not guarantee — state it at exactly this strength (§0.3 item 50).** It guarantees **support-identity**: the shipped refit and every scored fold use the *same factor set* — same estimated members, same pinned members. It does **not** guarantee **vector-identity**: the gate's ΔMAE evidence comes from **per-fold, train-only** coefficient vectors, whereas `wFinal` is an **all-rows refit that no fold scored out of sample**. So the correct claim is *"the shipped vector was estimated on the same support the gate measured"*, **not** *"the shipped vector is the one the gate measured."* What the fixed support rules out is the specific failure it was introduced to rule out: shipping an exponent for a factor that some fold held at 1, or pinning one that some fold estimated.

   **One bounded exception, reported not assumed:** §4's graceful degenerate-scale neutralization can hold a globally-retained factor at 1 **on a single fold**, so that fold scored a strictly smaller support. Support-identity is asserted **at the selection level**; the per-fold departures are published as `foldNeutralization` (§7). A position where neutralization fired materially is **not** a clean support-identity claim — read that block before citing this item.
1a. **The exponents were fitted against the clamped objective — do not move the clamp (§1, §0.3 item 54).** Both arms of the gate apply the app's own `clamp(combinedNewFactorRaw, 0.67, 1.50)` (`seasonProjection.js:598`) to the enveloped sub-product before it reaches `rawPPG`. Activation must therefore raise the exponents **inside** that envelope — `combinedNewFactorRaw` becomes `Π fᵢ^{wᵢ}` over its enveloped members, still clamped to `[0.67, 1.50]`, with `shareTrend` and `regression` exponentiated **outside** it at `:599`. **Do not widen, remove, or relocate the envelope to accommodate a fitted exponent**: the app's own note already calls the headroom thin at ten factors ("worst-case theoretical stack ≈ 1.46 < 1.50 … do NOT re-widen", `:587-589`), and exponents > 1 push the product further out than the measurement that produced that note assumed. If a shipped vector makes the envelope bind materially in production, that is a finding to route back through a graded gate, not a rail to loosen. The verdict reports the fitted-arm clamp-hit rate (§7) precisely so this is known before activation, not after.
2. Exponents are **values-only** — no `factors` key added/renamed → no snapshot schemaVersion bump, nothing for `register-snapshots.mjs`, `NUMERIC_FACTOR_KEYS` untouched (§11).
3. Provisional (reduced-pipeline + age-blind gate; roadmap D-1) — re-validate at R4. **Carry the §0.3 fidelity gap and the §3.0-C residual forward.** The exponents were fitted in **half-PPR units** — the units the app's store-served projection is denominated in (§3.0-C3) — so they transport as-is; if the app ever re-scores `careerStats` under league scoring, re-run the fit.
4. **The exponents apply to the veteran path only** — the rookie path hardcodes/omits every fitted factor (§3.0-A), so the activation must not touch `rookieProjection`.
5. Do NOT activate `airYardsShare` (R3-EFFACT, gated on R1-AGE) or `shareLevel` (its 2026-08-08 CLEARS is a separate finding requiring its own gate — header scope note).

## 9. Tests to add

New `test/panel-fit.test.mjs` (pure-lib) + additions to `test/panel-integration.test.mjs`, `node --test`, run by `npm test`. Fixtures under `test/fixtures/`. *(Note: `0396050` already updated `test/panel.test.mjs` and `test/panel-integration.test.mjs` for the entity filter; those edits stand — the tests below are additive.)*

- **T-F1 reparameterization identity + the two-clamp structure (§1, §0.3 item 54):** `α→∞` drives `w → 1`; `w≡1` reproduces `predHand` exactly. **Clamp structure:** (a) on a row whose enveloped sub-product sits inside `[0.67,1.50]`, `predFitted` equals `anchorBasePPG · outer · inner` with `inner` un-truncated — i.e. the two-clamp form reduces to the flat product, so the change is inert where it should be; (b) construct a row where `w > 1` pushes the enveloped sub-product **above 1.50** while the hand product stays inside, and assert `predFitted` is **truncated** (strictly below the unclamped value) while `predHand` is not — this is the exact configuration the fix exists for, and the one that biases ΔMAE if the envelope is skipped; (c) assert `shareTrend` and `regression` are **outside** the envelope — a row whose `shareTrend` alone would carry the product past 1.50 is **not** truncated; (d) assert the two clamps are applied in order and not merged: a row clamped by the inner envelope and then again by the outer `[0,40]` yields the composed result, not either alone; (e) `clampHits` counts increment per arm exactly on the truncating rows.
- **T-F2 scale-corrected shrinkage:** two synthetic **orthogonal** factors with `log f` variances 10× apart and equal true effect → `w−1` shrunk by the same fraction `1/(1+α)`; a naive raw-`X` constant-λ fit shrinks them unequally. Assert `ridgeLambda === α·nTrain`.
- **T-F3 identifiability guard + verdict rules.**
  *On `selectFitFactors` (pure, no mocking):* (a) a column flat on ≥90% of the given rows is pinned and absent from `fitFactors`; (b) **the sentinel-blind case that motivated the rule** — a `regressionFactor`-shaped column with **zero** sentinel hits but a 0.95 flat-1.0 rate **is** pinned; (c) a column at 0.85 flat is **not** pinned; (d) **it ranges over `FIT_CANDIDATES[position]`, not `FULL_FACTORS[position]`** — for QB, `rzUsage` appears in neither `fitFactors` nor `pinned` however its column looks, and is returned under `heldInArm`; `flatOneRates` carries **every candidate**, retained ones included (§0.3 item 52).
  *On graceful degenerate scale in `fitExponents` (§0.3 items 47/57) — the corrected T-F3(d):* the old rationale ("a fully flat column is pinned by the single rule, so the scale predicate is unreachable for retained factors") was **false**; the reachable case is the **global-vs-fold mismatch**, since selection is global over `posRows` while `s_i` is per-fold on train rows. Assert directly: (i) construct a factor whose flat-1.0 rate over all `posRows` is **below** 0.90 — so `selectFitFactors` retains it — but which is **100% flat on one fold's train years**; run `evaluateExponentModel` and assert the run **completes**, that fold's `w[factor] === 1` exactly, `neutralized` carries `{factor, reason:'flatOnTrain'}`, that fold's `estimatedFactors` excludes it, and **every other fold still estimates it**; (ii) **the near-degenerate case the exact-zero trigger missed (§0.3 item 57)** — the same construction at **~95% flat on one fold's train rows** (so `s_i > 0` and the old trigger would stay silent) must **also** neutralize, `reason:'flatOnTrain'`, with the recorded `flatRate ≥ FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE`; add the contrast case at ~85% flat, which must **not** neutralize; (iii) hand `fitExponents` a synthetic column yielding `s_i = Infinity` and assert it neutralizes with `reason:'nonFiniteScale'` — **not** a throw (the `Number.isFinite` half, §0.3 item 41 as amended); (iv) assert **nothing throws** on any of these paths — an abort would kill the whole `--fit` run over one thin fold; (v) assert `foldNeutralization` aggregates both reasons separately, that a run with no degeneracy reports an all-zero block, and that `maxAbsWMinus1` is populated per fold; (vi) **the trigger reuses one constant at two scopes** — assert `selectFitFactors` and the fold trigger both read `FIT_MAX_FLAT_ONE_RATE`, so raising it in a test moves both.
  *On the fixed-set contract:* `gradeExponentFit` calls `selectFitFactors` **once** — assert (via a counting spy or by asserting `wByAlpha` entries share an identical estimated-key set) that the α-sweep does not re-select, and that `wFinal`'s estimated keys equal every fold's **selected** support. **Compare against the selection, not against each fold's `estimatedFactors`** — a fold that neutralized a factor legitimately has a smaller `estimatedFactors`, which is support-identity's one bounded exception (§8 item 1), not a violation.
  *On `decideFitVerdict` (which never sees flat rates, `nToParam`, or a sensitivity label — §0.3 item 49):* table-driven, one case per **base** label incl. ordering edges; α-sign-flip → UNSTABLE. Assert its return is always one of the four base labels and **never** `INSUFFICIENT-POWER`.
  *On the two other verdict channels:* (i) `gradeExponentFit` with `nToParam < 20` returns `verdict === 'INSUFFICIENT-POWER'` **and never calls `decideFitVerdict`** (counting spy) and performs no fit; (ii) `runFit`'s override — base `CLEARS` + sensitivity `NO-GAIN` → final `UNSTABLE`, with `baseVerdict`/`sensitivityVerdict` both preserved in the report; matching labels pass through unchanged.
  *On the product arms:* a pinned factor still appears in `wFinal` with `w === 1` and still contributes to **both** `predHand` and `predFitted` — construct a fit row where the pinned factor ≠ 1.0 and assert `predHand` ≠ the product that omits it.
- **T-F4 CV leakage (scales and coefficients only — the pin is global by design, §0.3 item 39):** exponents and RMS scales are computed from train rows only; an eval-year outlier changes neither `wByFold[i].w` nor `wByFold[i].scales`. Assert each fold's train set is `folds[i].trainYears`-derived (mirroring `evaluateModel:487-489`).
- **T-F5 reconstruction parity — golden fixtures, incl. every sentinel branch:** each `reconstruct*` returns the exact app-documented multiplier on its happy path **and** exactly 1.0 on each §3.0-B condition (momentum <4; trajectory <2; shareTrend <2 series entries; snapShare missing `off_snp`/`tm_off_snp ≤ 0`/QB/empty pool; rzUsage `opp ≤ 0`/empty pool; teamRzShare QB/`denom < 20`/**`opp < minOpp`**/absent team entry/empty pool). Plus the **non-sentinel** inversion trap: `regressionFactor` with <3 qualifying applies the **full undampened** correction, not 1.0 (§3.0-B2). **Plus the QB `rzUsage` cases (§0.3 item 48):** (i) a QB with `pass_att ≥ 50` returns a **real, non-1.0** factor off `RZ_CONFIG.QB` (`pass_rz_att`/`pass_att`, shrinkK **80**) — assert against a hand-computed value, and assert it is **not** the WR/RB config; (ii) an **absent `pass_rz_att` with positive `pass_att`** yields a genuine rate of **0** and a computed factor, **not** a sentinel and not a drop (`?? 0`, `usageMetrics.js:165`); (iii) `pass_att ≤ 0` or absent → the `opp` sentinel, exactly 1.0. Also assert the **flat-1.0 interval** for `regressionFactor` at its true edges: `outlierRatio` of 1.15 and 0.85 both give `1.00`, while **1.16 gives 0.95** and 1.36 gives **0.88** — the 1.16 case is the one that would pass under the retired `[0.85, 1.35]` reading, and the pair together pin the branch order (`>1.35` tested first, then `>1.15` catching `(1.15, 1.35]`; §0.3 items 51/63). **Plus `teamRzShare`'s in-module 3dp rounding (§0.3 item 56):** assert `reconstructTeamRzShareFactor` returns a value **rounded to 3dp** — construct inputs whose pre-round factor has ≥4 significant decimals and assert the exact rounded value, **and** a case in `[0.9995, 1.0005)` that must come back as exactly `1.000` and be counted in `flatOneCounts` with **no** sentinel taken. Contrast assertion: `reconstructSnapShareFactor`/`reconstructRzUsageFactor` return **unrounded** factors (the asymmetry is real — `usageMetrics.js` rounds only the rates).

## 11. Cross-repo impact

**New cross-repo MIRROR contract (the one real exposure):** `lib/projectionFactors.mjs` mirrors the app's factor transforms **and every upstream producer enumerated in §3.0** — `momentum.js`, `regressionSignals.js`, `teamContext.js` (`computeShareTrend`, **`computeHistoricalShares` — the share-series builder incl. the gp≥8 gate, the positive-own-volume requirement, the WR/TE `rec` fallback, the no-floor denominators and the 3dp rounding**, **`computeHistoricalTeamTotals` — the denominator builder incl. its `gamesPlayed ≥ 1` gate and `TEAM_*` entity filter**, `resolveAttributedTeam`), `usageMetrics.js` (cohort gates, `refSeason` pool rule, count shrinkage, sentinel returns, **the whole `RZ_CONFIG` table including `RZ_CONFIG.QB` — `pass_rz_att`/`pass_att`, `minOpp 50`, `shrinkK 80`, `:59` — and the `(stats[rzKey] ?? 0)` numerator coalescence at `:96`/`:165`**), `teamRzShare.js` (same + `MIN_TEAM_DENOM`, `minOpp`), and `seasonProjection.js` (the gp≥8 + finite-`fantasyPoints` `qualifying` list and `lastQ` selection `:283-304`/`:407-408`, the **rookie-vs-veteran routing** `:310`, the per-length basePPG weight table `:317-319` with its `wSum` division `:321-322`, the call-site team resolution `:488`, the forward-mover neutralization `:359-361`/`:493-497`, **and the combined-factor envelope `:594-601` — which factors enter `combinedNewFactorRaw`, the `[0.67, 1.50]` clamp, and which terms stay outside it**). **If the app changes any of these — a constant, a gate, a shrinkage K, a qualifying threshold, the routing condition, a sentinel branch, a series-construction branch, a denominator accumulator, or the cohort reference season — the fit reconstructs a factor the app no longer produces and the fitted exponents stop transporting.**

**A second structural dependency, distinct from the per-factor transforms (§0.3 item 54):** the mirror must track **how the app combines the factors**, not only how each one computes. `combinedNewFactorRaw`'s **membership** (which ten factors, `:594-597`) and the **`[0.67, 1.50]` envelope** (`:598`) are both load-bearing for the fit: membership decides the `inner`/`outer` partition, and the envelope is applied in both arms. **If the app adds or removes an envelope member, moves a factor across the envelope boundary, or changes the clamp range, the fit's arms stop matching the app's objective and the exponents must be re-fitted** — even if every individual factor transform is untouched. Name this in the contract row.

**One dependency this revision makes explicit (§0.3 item 48):** the mirror must track **which positions the app applies each factor to**, not only how each factor computes. `rzUsageFactor` is applied to **all four** positions (`computeUsageFactors` is not position-gated at its call site, `seasonProjection.js:476-479`; it enters `combinedNewFactorRaw` for every position, `:594-597`) — QB is *not* gated out the way it is for `snapShare` (`SNAP_POSITIONS`) and `teamRzShare` (`RZ_SHARE_CONFIG`). **If the app ever adds QB to a factor's gate, or removes it, the corresponding position's `F_p^full` here changes and its hand arm silently stops matching the app's** — which is precisely the defect item 48 fixed. Name the per-position applicability in the contract row alongside the function list.

**One additional mirror dependency, easy to miss:** the fit's basis choice (§3.0-C3) rests on the app reading store `fantasyPoints` **verbatim** (`src/api/sleeperStats.js:145-159`) and on this repo writing that field as half-PPR (`lib/sleeper.mjs:212, 240-243`). **If the app ever re-scores store-served `careerStats` under league scoring, or this repo changes `weeklyPoints`' source from `pts_half_ppr`, the fit's ppg series stops matching the app's and the exponents must be re-fitted.** Name this in the contract row alongside the function list.

Add a row to the data `CLAUDE.md` cross-repo contracts table (mirror the `calculateFantasyPoints` port row) naming the mirrored functions (transforms **and** input-pipeline producers), the routing/sentinel dependency, the half-PPR basis dependency, **and the two factors without end-to-end parity coverage**. Parity-guarded by `test/panel-fit.test.mjs` T-F5 + T-F17 + T-F18 + T-F10 (real-player, 5 of 7, half-PPR basis, through the exported builders) + T-F8/T-F11/T-F14/T-F16.

**Internal-only, not cross-repo:** `buildCohortPools` and `selectFitFactors` are new **data-repo** exports (§6.2). They mirror app *behaviour* (pool gates) but expose no served shape and create no obligation on the app. Likewise `isTeamAggregateId` (landed `0396050`, `lib/backtest.mjs:13`) is an independent mirror of the app's own copy, not a shared contract.

**Persisted factor keys touched by the fit:** none. The fit persists nothing to a served file. `scripts/grade-snapshot.mjs → buildHalfPprOutcomes`/`buildInBasisOutcomes` are reused **read-only** and unmodified. `lib/grade.mjs`'s `NUMERIC_FACTOR_KEYS` (31-58) is untouched. (The **activation** unit changes persisted factor *values* — see `r3fit-activation.md`.)

**Read-only reuse of app snapshots (benign):** T-F10 reads a committed snapshot's `factors` as reconstruction ground truth via a redacted fixture copy. Read-only; creates no contract obligation.

**No served-shape / manifest / scoring-math change.** `lib/fantasyPoints.mjs` untouched; the outcome builders reused read-only; no `bin/update.mjs` subcommand. The `rec` accumulator (§6.2) is internal to an analysis builder whose output is never serialized.

## 12. Step sequence for the implementer
